stories.title: Knicks’ Karl-Anthony Towns acting like ‘second coach’ sign of fixed Mike Brown partnership
stories.summary: A once rocky partnership has evolved into a trusting and collaborative relationship between Karl-Anthony Towns and Mike Brown.
stories.detailText: Karl-Anthony Towns' relationship with Mike Brown has improved since the start of their first season together. TORONTO — A once rocky partnership has evolved into a trusting and collaborative relationship between Karl-Anthony Towns and Mike Brown. Towns revealed Tuesday that Brown has been embracing his suggestions “like I’m a second coach,” which is a residual benefit of their success in the 2026 postseason. It’s amazing what a championship can do. “It’s more familiarity with the system and building that trust with Mike where he can trust me with things I see and say, which started in the playoffs,” Towns said. “So building off that this year. Having more input and him hearing me out.” Towns said he and the coach collaborate “a lot” during games. “Him trusting me like a second coach. Me and him are always coaching with each other in the game, looking at game plans and plays and maybe ideologies and things I see that can help our team win, especially in close games,” Towns said. “Working with him and coaching on the floor. It’s been great. It’s been fun.” Karl-Anthony Towns looks to make a play as Scottie Barnes defends during the Knicks-Raptors game on Nov. 17, 2026, in Toronto. NBAE via Getty Images It wasn’t always so harmonious between the coach and All-Star center. When Brown took over before last season, Towns’ production plummeted and it was clear the player-coach dynamic was off-kilter. As Towns said multiple times during last season’s struggles, “The system is different.” Towns also declared during the 2025 training camp that he didn’t know his role. It got messier by midseason, when Brown called out Towns in January for not recovering on defense after falling on a layup attempt. “When you fall down, you’ve got to get up and got to sprint down the floor,” Brown said at the time. “And even when you’re the last guy down the floor, you’ve got to get down there just in case there’s a long rebound. There was no urgency.” But then Brown placed Towns as an offensive hub in the playoffs, and the Knicks raised a banner because, among other reasons, the adjustment worked spectacularly. This season, Towns is off to the best start on the roster with averages of 21.6 points and 13.6 rebounds entering Tuesday’s game against the Raptors. He was shooting an efficient 53.4 percent from the field, and 39.7 percent from beyond the arc — both dramatic improvements from last season. CHECK OUT THE LATEST NBA STANDINGS AND KNICKS STATS Mike Brown shouts out instructions on the baseline during the fourth quarter of the Knicks’ loss to the Cavaliers on Nov. 11, 2026, at Madison Square Garden. Charles Wenzelberg / New York Post Not coincidentally, he’s in a better place with his head coach. “We just grew. We’ve grown with each other,” Towns said. “And obviously there’s trust that has to be established and both of us trust each other a lot. And the last playoff run showed it. So just building off that trust and the relationship that was built in the playoffs and having it make our team better this year.” Brown agreed they’re in a better place and he’s given KAT ownership of the adjustments. “It’s just part of being around each other,” Brown said. “You hope your relationship with everybody grows. That’s not gonna always happen but you hope it does. KAT’s got a really good feel of how to play the game. Obviously he’s a perennial All-Star. So those things you’ve always got to take into account when it comes to trying to listen or try to adapt more to what their style of play is. “As a head coach — come in, it’s your first year, and you have an idea what you want to do. Sometimes it doesn’t fit. Offensively, or defensively. And that’s when you’ve got to pivot. And so we kept pivoting and pivoting and building until we found a nice little groove. We feel pretty good about each other right now.”

stories.title: Jose Alvarado making Knicks presence felt — even if he’s not on court
stories.summary: Without playing time, Jose Alvarado has channeled his energy into being the No. 1 Knicks supporter.
stories.detailText: TORONTO — Without playing time, Jose Alvarado has channeled his energy into being the No. 1 Knicks supporter. The third-string point guard has been, by far, the most boisterous and engaged Knick on the bench despite being pulled from the rotation a couple of weeks ago . “I think it’s more how I was raised [by] my parents,” Alvarado said. “Treat people how you want to be treated. Sometimes the situation isn’t going to be what you want. You can’t control certain things and control what you can and that’s your attitude, your energy every day. So I try to do that. Jose Alvarado greets forward Mohamed Diawara as he walks back to the bench during the Knicks’ blowout win over the Bucks on Nov. 10, 2026, at Madison Square Garden. Charles Wenzelberg / New York Post “I’m human, I have days where it’s not going to be all lovey-dovey. But I always tell myself, ‘Whether I’m not playing or not, I got the best seats in the house.’ And I get to support my teammates. So I try to go with that mindset as best I can and my teammates allow me to be myself.” In a viral moment from Sunday’s victory over the Raptors , Alvarado was filmed comforting a visibly dejected Mikal Bridges, who was struggling and on the bench. Alvarado said it was a common scene that just happened to be televised. He was also spotted Tuesday giving advice to Tyler Kolek, the player who supplanted Alvarado in the rotation. “[Mikal] is fine. We are all human,” Alvarado said. “The camera caught us that time, but I probably do stuff like that 100 times during a game.” Jose Alvarado looks on during the Knicks’ win over the Nets on Nov. 2, 2026, at Madison Square Garden. NBAE via Getty Images Karl-Anthony Towns lauded Alvarado’s impact. “Jose is a consummate professional. He’s probably one of the best locker room guys we have, and one of the best people we have on the bench,” Towns said. “His energy, just his presence, with a jersey on or a warmup on, it means more for this team than what the stats show.” Alvarado signed a three-year, $14.4 million contract in the summer to return to the Knicks, but suffered an early ankle sprain and lost his role to the more offensive-minded Kolek. Alvarado entered Tuesday night against the Raptors with zero appearances longer than 10 minutes since Oct. 23. “The season is long,” Alvarado said. “I’ve been on the other side. When I first got in the league [in 2021], I wasn’t even touching the court. Then eventually I got to touch the court and get some reps in and played a huge role in the rotation. “Sometimes you get out of it. The only way to get back is stay ready because an opportunity is going to come, you just don’t know when. So that’s the hardest thing is the guessing game of when that will happen. But you work, work and work and trust that it will come in the end of the day.” Work and cheer.

stories.title: Miami Heat unveil 'A Night in Vice City' court, activities ahead of GTA VI release
stories.summary: With Grand Theft Auto VI's long-awaited release date Thursday, the Heat are partnering with Rockstar Games to offer a topical lead-up event the night before.
stories.detailText: The Miami Heat have been carefully leaning into "Vice City" branding for years now , but 2026 will bring the team's most ambitious effort yet: Wednesday will be "A Night in Vice City" at the Kaseya Center. With Grand Theft Auto VI's long-awaited release date set for Thursday, the Heat are partnering with Rockstar Games to offer a topical lead-up event the night before. Miami is rolling out plenty of offerings, including before and during the game. Fans are encouraged to arrive early with with the team's "Vice City" collection available starting two hours before tipoff. There will be GTA VI-inspired cars set outside Kaseya Center on the West Plaza plus a GTA IV logo next to the rides for pictures. Similar spots for photos will be scattered throughout the arena and East Plaza. Official music from the game is going to be played in-arena, while Cluckin' Bell and Burger Joint -- two fast food restaurants from the GTA series -- will be at select concessions in Kaseya Center. The night will feature a special Vice-themed court and a reimagined edition of the team's popular alternate uniforms. Even the roof of Kaseya Center is going to be altered to read: "Welcome to Vice City." Miami revealed the pink, white and blue hardwood court Tuesday, featuring "Vice City" in the center and "I heart Vice City" on a baseline. The "VI" logo also appears near the dunker spot on each side of the court. The jerseys, unveiled on Nov. 6., build on the team's past "Vice" alternates with nods to Grand Theft Auto VI and Travis Scott's Cactus Jack brand. The black Swingman jersey features pink and white accents, "Vice City" across the chest, Scott's signature flipped Nike Swoosh and a "VI" nod to the game. Six pink stars and Cactus Jack branding appear at the hem alongside a tag featuring Rockstar Games, the Heat and Cactus Jack. Both the on-court and Swingman versions will be available in limited quantities Wednesday. According to a news release, the special occasion will "transform the Kaseya Center into Vice City -- showcasing the Miami-inspired setting of Grand Theft Auto VI -- for a first-of-its-kind sports crossover experience." The Heat kicked off the promotion for the special event on Nov. 5., lighting up the "Welcome to Vice City" signage on the roof of its arena. Players have expressed excitement, including Giannis Antetokounmpo and Klay Thompson , an avid gamer. "I understand the hype and feel like a lot of people in this locker room have played the game. They're excited for the game to come out," Antetokounmpo said Monday. "Just be able to be part of one of the most talked about video games. It's fun. I heard that we have special jerseys and special court, so I'm excited for that, excited for the energy." Antetokounmpo added that the main thing for the Heat though is that they come out and win. Thompson revealed Monday that he has been playing GTA since it was "the bird's-eye view," which was the set up for the earlier editions over 20 years ago. Therefore, even at 36 years old, Thompson said he will still be gaming once he gets this version and expressed excitement over the story mode. He also joked about potentially streaming himself playing GTA VI while wearing the special "Vice City" threads. "I'm excited when that game does come out. ... It will feel much better to have a day of gaming when we get that victory on Wednesday. That will feel so much better," he said . The Heat ring in "A Night in Vice City" with a matchup against the Milwaukee Bucks Wednesday on ESPN.

stories.title: Nets’ free-throw problem on full display in loss to 76ers
stories.summary: The Brooklyn Nets shot just 64.7% from the free-throw line in a 135-123 loss to the 76ers, dropping them to 3-10 on the season.
stories.detailText: Julius Randle (30) of the Brooklyn Nets shoots a free throw against the Philadelphia 76ers in Brooklyn, N.Y., Monday, Nov. 16, 2026. The Nets have been a bottom five team in the NBA this season from the free-throw line, and they certainly left too many points at the stripe in Monday’s loss to the 76ers . The Nets shot just 22-for-34 for a 64.7 percent conversion rate in their 12-point defeat. For the season, Brooklyn is ranked 26th in the league at 74.8 percent through its 3-10 start. “Once again, I don’t want to go to the players and be like, ‘We gotta make free throws,’ because then you go there and you’re nervous,” Nets coach Jordi Fernández said. Jaylen Brown of the Philadelphia 76ers dribbles against Julius Randle of the Brooklyn Nets in New York, Monday, Nov. 16, 2026. The 76ers won 135-123. Getty Images “Obviously I don’t want to shoot 64 percent. … If we shoot better, we probably have a bigger chance. But I know our guys are good shooters and they’re gonna make free throws. We gotta concentrate and make sure that we believe that all of them are going to go in.” Nolan Traore, Michael Porter Jr. and Julius Randle were a combined 19-for-21 from the line, but Egor Dëmin, Day’Ron Sharpe, Moritz Wagner and Danny Wolf combined to miss nine of 10 attempts. Randle cut his lip in a face-to-face collision in Monday’s fourth quarter with Philly’s Jaylen Brown, who temporarily left the game to get his face bandaged. Brown also suffered a hamstring injury after returning to the floor. “I’m fine. It feels terrible, to be honest. But I’m fine,” Randle said. “I just went to trap him and he turned, and he didn’t see me. Just kind of collided, but it’s fine.” Julius Randle (30) of the Brooklyn Nets shoots a free throw against the Philadelphia 76ers in Brooklyn, N.Y., Monday, Nov. 16, 2026. NBAE via Getty Images NBA legend Julius “Dr. J” Erving and former Nets coach Kevin Loughery will highlight the alumni present for a ceremony at halftime of Wednesday’s game against the Bulls honoring the Nets’ 1974 and 1976 ABA championship teams as part of the franchise’s 60th season. Others scheduled to attend include: Brian Taylor, Bill Melchionni, George Bucci, Jim Eakins, Rich Jones, Jim O’Brien, Billy Schaeffer, Al Skinner and Chuck Terry. Nets rookie Mikel Brown Jr. launched a mentorship program called “Mikel’s Crew” with a basketball clinic Tuesday with Brooklyn students from El Puente Beacon Leadership Center at MS 50 in Williamsburg. “I feel like that’s just what it’s all about: influencing the youth and the community the right way,” Brown said. “That’s just how I grew up. I was influenced, I had a lot of mentors and people in my corner that kind of shaped me into who I am today.”

stories.title: Lakers’ trust in starter’s defensive gambles paying off
stories.summary: Matisse Thybulle is a significant reason why the Lakers force a lot of turnovers.
stories.detailText: Matisse Thybulle’s explanation for how he steals passes midair while opponents try to get the ball up the court is simple. Even if the act of stealing the pass like a free safety intercepts a quarterback isn’t. Los Angeles Lakers guard Matisse Thybulle (4) steals the ball from the Sacramento Kings during an NBA game, Wednesday, Nov. 4, 2026, in Sacramento, Calif. AP Photo/Scott Marshall “I just look at the person passing; I just make eye contact with them,” Thybulle said after Tuesday’s shootaround ahead of the Lakers’ home game against the Hornets. “Because most guys aren’t really throwing no-look passes. Like Luka [Dončić], [Nikola] Jokić, there’s a couple guys in the league who really throw nowhere passes, especially in transition. “So if you just look people in their eyes, they’re going to look where they’re throwing the ball. I can just get a sense from the eye contact.” Matisse Thybulle of the Los Angeles Lakers blocks a shot by Devin Booker of the Phoenix Suns on Sunday, Nov. 15, 2026, in Phoenix, Arizona. Getty Images Again, simple. But if everyone was able to pick off passes like Thybulle, who’s shown a knack for playing the passing lanes throughout his eight-year NBA career, then they would. So what makes him more equipped at picking off passes in a way that looks easy? “Just being willing to take the risk,” he said. “I’ve missed a bunch of gambles as well as getting some. So just being willing to take the risk of assuming that where they’re looking is in fact where the guy is trying to pass the ball to.” The Lakers have benefited from the defensive gambles the 6-foot-5 wing takes. They entered Tuesday leading the league in defensive turnover percentage (18.7), according to Cleaning The Glass, and Thybulle is a significant reason. He entered Tuesday ranked No. 2 in the league in total steals (31) and deflections (60). Giannis Antetokounmpo shoots against Matisse Thybulle, left, and Austin Reaves during an NBA basketball game Monday, Nov. 2, 2026, in Los Angeles. AP Photo/Jayne Kamin-Oncea “Me and [assistant] coach Greg [St. Jean] have talked a lot about that — just trying to find ways for me to be me within the foundation of our defense,” Thybulle said. “And they like me gambling because it generates turnovers, whether I’m getting the steal. It’s just a matter of doing it in ways where our defense can absorb the mistake, if you will. If I do it in ways where our defense is structured to be able to absorb it, then it’s something that we can just use, and I try to use to give us an advantage.” The Lakers empowering Thybulle to take advantage of his defensive freedom, similar to how Dončić takes advantage of his offensive freedom, goes back to trust that was established during the preseason and training camp. “It can be challenging at times to play with someone like me who’s taking a lot of risks, gambling, getting out of position and sometimes throwing off the team defense,” he said. “And it can be really easy for them to just be like, ‘Well, Matisse keeps messing up our defense. Like, what the hell is he doing?’ But they understand and they let me learn from my mistakes.” He continued: “I gamble and sometimes I don’t get the pass, but sometimes I get a steal on the back end. There’s just the rapport that’s grown through that.”

stories.title: Rough Hawks injury news: CJ McCollum out 4 weeks (calf strain), Asa Newell likely out for season (toe)
stories.summary: McCollum had been providing scoring punch off the bench for Atlanta.
stories.detailText: This is rough injury news for Atlanta, which at 8-6 sits tied for the 4/5 seeds in the East: • Guard CJ McCollum suffered a strained left calf and will be reevaluated in four weeks, the team announced. • Big man Asa Newell has surgery to repair a left great toe hyperextension, and while the Hawks' announcement says he will be re-evaluated in four months, that will be mid-March, weeks away from the end of the regular season (April 11). It's unlikely we see Newell again this season. A player health update presented by @emoryhealthcare : CJ McCollum sustained a left leg injury during Sunday’s game at Milwaukee. Following a medical evaluation and imaging, he has been diagnosed with a left calf strain. McCollum will be re-evaluated in approximately four… pic.twitter.com/NgPzv12YmA — Atlanta Hawks (@ATLHawks) November 17, 2026 After eight games as a starter to open the season, McCollum was moved to a bench role in favor of rookie Kingston Flemmings (who has made the most of that opportunity). McCollum has accepted and thrived in his bench role, averaging 14.9 points per game (scoring 20+ in each of his last three appearances), and shooting 37% from 3. Atlanta is going to miss his scoring punch off the bench. Expect Corey Kispert to get extra run and touches with McCollum out. Newell was poised for a bigger role this season after bouncing between the Hawks and their G League affiliate last season. However, he played in just five games this season before the toe injury and never really got the chance to show how much his game had grown. That said, the Hawks had already picked up his option for next season, so he isn't going anywhere. Newell joins a few injured frontcourt Hawks players: Rookie center Henri Veesaar is out for the season with a torn ACL, while Mouhamed Gueye is out at least another month following foot surgery.

stories.title: 76ers' Jaylen Brown (hamstring) to miss Wednesday's game vs. Magic
stories.summary: Philadelphia 76ers forward Jaylen Brown will miss Wednesday's game against the Orlando Magic with a left hamstring strain, the Sixers announced Tuesday afternoon.
stories.detailText: Philadelphia 76ers forward Jaylen Brown will miss Wednesday's road game against the Orlando Magic with a left hamstring strain, the team said Tuesday. Brown will be reevaluated ahead of Saturday's home matchup against the Milwaukee Bucks , a source told ESPN. LeBron James , who missed the Sixers' 135-123 win over the Nets on Monday with low back management, has no injury designation for the Magic game. Brown exited late in the fourth quarter of Monday's win with the hamstring strain. It was one of two injuries he suffered in the game, in which he tied his season-high of 31 points and added 13 rebounds. In the first quarter he bumped heads with forward Julius Randle and was left bleeding on the court, in a tense moment that saw both benches circle around him. Wednesday night will be the second game Brown has missed this season. His only other absence was the Sixers' NBA Cup victory over the New York Knicks on Oct. 30, where he sat out with left knee soreness. Brown has found his stride in recent weeks, with back-to-back 31-point games in the Sixers' past two wins. He is averaging 24.6 points this month, 4.8 more than October; his field goal percentage in November is 53.7%, up from 43.6% last month. "I'm feeling a little bit more comfortable ... starting to feel a little bit more at home," Brown said Monday night. Big men Adem Bona (neck) and Dominick Barlow (back) are also out against the Magic. Barlow hasn't played yet this season.

Neemias Queta, who missed Monday’s game to rest, is fully available. Boston is coming off a 115-105 loss to the Orlando Magic, just its second loss in 13 games. The Celtics recovered from a sloppy first half to tie the game at 80, but Orlando scored 40 points in the fourth quarter to pull away. “We fought our asses off to get it to a one-possession game,” Joe Mazzulla said after the loss. “We take the lead, I think it’s 80 to 80. There are three or four plays that we don’t come up with that turn into catch-and-shoot threes or a layup for them. Those are the ones that you focus on.” Orlando did most of its damage inside, outscoring Boston 54-32 in the paint. Queta’s presence was sorely missed, and Paul George said that the team did not defend as well as they should have. “If anything, maybe we overrespected them behind the three-point line,” George said. “We knew Orlando was a paint team. They like to drive and get to the rim. They got a lot of guys that kind of put their head down and get to the rim. So we kind of played into their strengths. So that’s on us.” The loss came on the second night of a back-to-back, after the Celtics jumped out to a 42-9 first-quarter lead against the Dallas Mavericks on Sunday and ultimately won by 37. Mazzulla said the team didn’t overreact to the Mavericks win nor the Magic loss. “We weren’t jumping around for joy last night,” he said. “I mean, again, you can’t coach to the scoreboard.” Now the Celtics turn their attention to Denver “There’s a lot of things we obviously can learn from, and going on the road tomorrow,” Tatum said. “So obviously, probably watching film and regroup and just get ready for Denver.” The Nuggets are 7-5 and coming off a Monday night loss to the Phoenix Suns. They’re been better on the road (5-2) than at home (2-3). Jamal Murray leads the way with 26.1 points and 6 assists per game, while Nikola Jokic averages 24.1 points, 10.9 rebounds, and 8.9 assists. Celtics-Nuggets tips off at 9:30pm ET.

stories.title: Preview: Can the Utah Jazz finally get their second win vs. the LA Clippers?
stories.summary: Can the Utah Jazz finally pick up their second win?
stories.detailText: SALT LAKE CITY, UTAH - NOVEMBER 15: Keyonte George #3 of the Utah Jazz reacts during the final seconds of their loss to the San Antonio Spurs at the Delta Center on November 15, 2026 in Salt Lake City, Utah. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and or using this photograph, User is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement.(Photo by Chris Gardner/ Getty Images) | Getty Images There aren’t many NBA franchises that have ever felt more hopeless than the Los Angeles Clippers in the aftermath of the Kawhi Leonard-Steve Balmer saga. They went all-in on the concept of Leonard alongside All-Star wing Paul George, mortgaging the house, the dog, and even undergoing construction of a state-of-the-art arena in which they could showcase their prosperous future. Instead, that core imploded. Leonard and George have both departed, and the Clippers were stripped of five first-round picks, with bans, suspensions, and fines abound. It’s a team without a future. Without hope for organic improvement. Without allure for potential free agent signings. So yeah, times are feeling a bit shallow in this shadowy corner of LA. If anyone can relate to such a feeling of hopelessness, it’s the Utah Jazz. After four long years in the tanking pressure cooker, Utah’s rebuilt product still came out half-baked. Losers of 12 straight, a veteran (expensive) frontcourt spending more time on the injury report than the basketball court, and good for at least one baffling implosion per game, Will Hardy’s team is 1-13, tied for the worst record in the entire NBA, and light-years removed from the playoff hunt that had been promised pre-season. Utah’s young core has been underwhelming outside of Darryn Peterson, Keyonte George, and Ace Bailey. In all truth, Peterson’s is the only name in that trio whose development has taken a clear and obvious upward trajectory. George’s scoring efficiency and decision-making have fluctuated in quality, and his defensive impact remains minimal. Bailey’s mastered the Warriors-era Shaun Livingston mid-range pull-up, but can’t seem to hit his target from beyond the arc, shooting just over 26% on the young season. Despite keeping the score tight against some of the best teams in the West, Utah still has no winning experience. When the game clock hits winning time, the Jazz’s watches are unsynchronized. The host Clippers, currently 4-8, are 6.5-point favorites at the time of this article. If the Jazz can’t find a way to win this one, it’s difficult to imagine where they might collect their second win of the season. Calvin Barrett is the Associate Editor for SLC Dunk and a Utah Jazz columnist for the Standard-Examiner. Originally from Springville, Utah, he currently writes from his desk in Japan.

stories.title: Raptors say Kawhi Leonard progressing but out at least another week
stories.summary: The Raptors said Tuesday that while Kawhi Leonard is progressing in his recovery from left knee swelling, he will remain out for at least another week.
stories.detailText: The Toronto Raptors said Tuesday that while Kawhi Leonard is progressing in his recovery from left knee swelling, he will remain out for at least another week. Leonard, who has been sidelined since Oct. 23, "has progressed in his strength and conditioning program," and another update will be provided in a week, the team said. The seven-time All-Star will miss four more games before the next scheduled update; he has already missed 11 games this season while appearing in just two in his first campaign back with the Raptors. Leonard, 35, had an MRI on his knee last month that showed no structural damage. He previously had issues with his right knee, having multiple surgeries for his meniscus and ACL. Leonard is averaging 19.5 points, 7.5 rebounds and 3.5 steals in his two games played in his second stint with Toronto. He was traded to the Raptors from the LA Clippers this offseason following a scandal-marred conclusion to his six seasons in Los Angeles. He agreed to a two-year, $115 million contract extension with the Raptors after the trade.

stories.title: Indiana Fever GM search narrows, multiple candidates come with NBA ties: Sources
stories.summary: The Indiana Fever’s search for a new general manager is ramping up. The franchise is expected to evaluate several finalists, including many with NBA backgrounds, and make a hire in the next few weeks, according to multiple sources familiar with the search who were granted anonymity because they are not permitted to sp…
stories.detailText: The Indiana Fever’s search for a new general manager is ramping up. The franchise is expected to evaluate several finalists, including many with NBA backgrounds, and make a hire in the next few weeks, according to multiple sources familiar with the search who were granted anonymity because they are not permitted to speak publicly about the search process. Among the list of candidates being considered are Sacramento Kings vice president of basketball operations and player personnel Phil Jabour, Boston Celtics vice president of team operations and organizational growth Allison Feaster and former Dallas Mavericks assistant general manager Matt Ricardi. Clare Duwelius, former Minnesota Lynx basketball operations manager and current Unrivaled general manager and executive vice president, was also being considered at one point in the search process. The Fever’s front office overhaul began on Oct. 23 when the franchise announced longtime president Kelly Krauskopf would step down after three decades with Pacers Sports & Entertainment. She informed leadership of her decision before the end of the 2026 season. Later that same day news broke that the Fever had f ired general manager Amber Cox after two seasons. Cox’s firing followed her heavily scrutinized exit interview, during which she was dismissive of critiques of the Fever fan base. Four-time All-Star Kelsey Mitchell shared comments during the same session that directly contradicted Cox, detailing difficulties of competing for fans who she said “that may not like you .” She added that the organization is “unbelievable,” but said it hasn’t been easy “trying to be yourself.” Fever coach Stephanie White has one year left on her contract and is expected to remain in her position, according to a source familiar with discussions who spoke on the condition of anonymity to preserve relationships. White represented the Fever at last week’s WNBA competition committee meeting, which includes league leadership along with coaches and general managers from every team. The Fever shakeup was the first step in what is expected to be one of the most critical free agency periods in the franchise’s history that starts with an attempt to re-sign Mitchell who is an unrestricted free agent. The Fever also will look to extend three-time All-Star Caitlin Clark under the league’s new EPIC (Exceptional Performance on Initial Contract) clause. A highly anticipated lever in the league’s new collective bargaining agreement, the EPIC clause allows players signed to their rookie scale contract who have been named MVP or to an All-WNBA first or second team to renegotiate the final year of their rookie contract to sign a multi-year extension. Four-time All-Star Aliyah Boston signed an extension under the EPIC provision in April, keeping her with the franchise through 2029. Despite boasting the top offense in the league, powered by record breaking seasons from Mitchell and Clark, the Fever were bounced by the Las Vegas Aces in the first round of the playoffs. The Fever have failed to make it past the semifinals since drafting Clark with the No. 1 overall pick in 2024. Pacers Sports & Entertainment hired Excel Search & Advisory to lead the search for a new Fever general manager. The firm is also leading the league’s search for a new commissioner. Clark is represented by the agency’s sports management sector. Riccardi, who worked in the Brooklyn Nets organization in a variety of roles from 2010 to 2022, was with the Dallas Mavericks from 2022 to 2026. He spent most of his last year there as the interim co-general manager, and had been elevated from his assistant general manager position when former president of basketball operations Nico Harrison was fired from his post. Riccardi was a finalist to replace Harrison, but the job ultimately went to Masai Ujiri. Feaster, a Harvard graduate and three-time Ivy League Player of the Year, was drafted fifth overall by the Los Angeles Sparks in 1998 and finished her WNBA career with the Fever in 2008. (She played overseas until retiring in 2016.) She joined the Celtics as their director of player development in September 2019 and was later promoted to vice president of player development and organizational growth. Jabour, who has been with the Sacramento Kings since October 2020, is their vice president of basketball operations and player personnel. He has spent two decades in the NBA, previously with Houston, Orlando and Philadelphia in a variety of roles. The Fever are one of nine WNBA franchises with varying levels of shared ownership with an NBA franchise. Conversations around both leagues about their GM search have included an expectation that the Fever will operate more closely in line with their NBA counterpart. That is already being reflected in the franchise’s $78 million investment into a state-of-the-art practice facility which is scheduled to open this coming spring, but also in their comprehensive team staffing. stories.title: Ramona Shelburne doubles down on inaccurate Lakers take
stories.summary: Ramona Shelburne gave her honest thoughts on the Lakers this season. “It’s easy to find your way when you’re playing one of the easiest schedules in the league,” Shelburne said...
stories.detailText: Ramona Shelburne gave her honest thoughts on the Lakers this season. “It’s easy to find your way when you’re playing one of the easiest schedules in the league,” Shelburne said on ESPN. Luka Doncic (77) and Austin Reaves (15) of the Los Angeles Lakers look on during a game against the Toronto Raptors on Sunday, Nov. 1, 2026, in Los Angeles. NBAE via Getty Images While Los Angeles’ 12-2 record hasn’t come by defeating all the NBA’s best teams, the Lakers’ early strength of schedule ranks around 14th to 16th. That means the cumulative strength of schedule is around league average, not one of the easiest as Shelburne implied. NBA on ESPN’s post of Shelburne’s take was not received well by many as a Community Note was added, stating: “Analyses rank the Lakers’ played schedule near average or slightly easier than league average in strength, not one of the easiest; Spurs and Memphis rank easier per opponent records and models.” “It’s easy to find your way when you’re playing one of the easiest schedules in the league.” — @ramonashelburne on the Los Angeles Lakers after their 12-2 start. pic.twitter.com/Fl1OlBd8jC — NBA on ESPN (@ESPNNBA) November 16, 2026 Shelburne chose to defend her take the following day and went on an unfiltered rant on ESPN’s radio show Tuesday morning. “I don’t think people understand what it’s like to be a female reporter,” Shelburne said. “It’s an objective thing here that they have not played any of the top teams in the West yet.” Shelburne’s assessment is correct; the Lakers have not played a juggernaut like the Spurs or Rockets. But as the saying goes, you can only beat what’s in front of you. The Lakers’ early-season schedule has featured more teams above .500 than the Spurs have faced. and LA has won more of those games. But fans were quick to criticize Shelburne. “ummmm what…??? this is not a male/female thing ,” one X user said. “You were factually wrong, got a community note, just apologize and move on,” another user wrote on X. For many, the NBA insider’s Lakers reporting has drawn skepticism in recent years. ESPN’s Ramona Shelburne attends The Annual espnW: Women + Sports Summit day 1 at The Lodge at Torrey Pines on October 18, 2021. Getty Images Fans have been critical of her MVP voting history, including her past ballots in which she ranked Luka Doncic at No. 4. In 2023, she placed Jalen Brunson at No. 2 over Doncic in the fourth spot. ESPN’s John Ireland said Shelburne is an apologist for the Clippers, which could contribute to her seemingly one-sided opinion on their crosstown rivals. “You are an apologist for the Clippers,” Ireland told Shelburne last December on ESPN LA. “And you’re not the only one.” “Yeah,” Shelburne conceded. Los Angeles Lakers’ Austin Reaves shrugs during the first half of an NBA basketball game against the Milwaukee Bucks, Wednesday, Nov. 11, 2026, in Milwaukee. AP Photo/Aaron Gash “For whatever reason, the media is in love with the [Clippers] front office,” Ireland said. Shelburne remains a brilliant writer and respected NBA insider, but her reporting on the Lakers, at times, lights a fire under fans.

stories.title: Jaylen Brown to miss 76ers game Wednesday vs. Magic due to 'hamstring strain'
stories.summary: Brown finished Monday's win over Brooklyn with 31 points, his current season-high.
stories.detailText: The Philadelphia 76ers will take on the Orlando Magic on Wednesday night, but without star shooting guard Jaylen Brown. He is dealing with a hamstring strain and has already been ruled out for tomorrow night's game. Brown picked up the injury during Philadelphia's win over the Brooklyn Nets on Monday. The guard is in his first season with the 76ers after the infamous trade that sent him to Philadelphia from Boston. Brown has played in 14 games so far this season and is averaging 22.6 points, 6.6 rebounds, and 3.6 assists. The Philadelphia guard had a slow start with his new team, scoring 19 points in his team debut. The 76ers have tried to find the best fit among Joel Embiid, Tyrese Maxey, Brown, and free-agent signee LeBron James. It finally seemed to be clicking for Brown ahead of the injury. He logged back-to-back games with 31 points, his season high. The guard finished Monday night's win with a double-double: 31 points and 13 rebounds. He shot just 47.4% from the field, but he made 10 of 11 attempts from the charity stripe as Philadelphia beat Brooklyn 135-123. Without Brown in the lineup, the 76ers will likely give more minutes to Kentavious Caldwell-Pope and Jabari Walker. Wednesday's game against Orlando will be Brown's second missed game this season. He also missed Philly's first game of a back-to-back against the New York Knicks. Brown was dealing with both a head and a hamstring injury coming out of Monday's win against Brooklyn. After the game, he said that he may have to get imaging done on Tuesday. Brown has been diagnosed with a left hamstring strain, but it remains unclear whether it will keep him out beyond Wednesday's game. Philadelphia has the Magic, Milwaukee Bucks, Portland Trail Blazers, Miami Heat, and Indiana Pacers in its next five games.

NBA Trade Lab: Dejounte Murray's trade request After formally requesting a trade last Friday , New Orleans Pelicans guard Dejounte Murray has unsurprisingly been the player most involved in fan-created trades over the past seven days in our NBA Trade Lab . The Spurs traded Murray to the Hawks in 2022 for a massive haul: three first-round picks (including the Hawks' pick in the upcoming 2027 draft) and one first-round pick swap. At the time, Murray was viewed as a burgeoning young star with a strong impact on both sides of the ball. In Atlanta he expanded his offensive game, but his defensive impact, as measured by Net Points , fell off a cliff. In 2024, the Hawks sent him to the Pelicans in exchange for a package that included two first-round picks and Dyson Daniels , who went on to win Most Improved Player the following season . Now in 2026, it appears likely Murray will be on the move again, but his market is difficult to read. His impact metrics have been on the decline, and he's making over $30 million for the next two seasons after turning 30 years old. At the same time, he is undoubtedly a talented player who could certainly find a renaissance in the right situation. Let's look at some of the top fan-created trades to see what fans are thinking might be a realistic deal. Trade No. 1 Pelicans get: Jalen Green Phoenix Suns get: Dejounte Murray Green and Murray are similar in many ways, so a straight-up swap could make sense for both teams. Green is a talented scorer, but he lacks consistency and doesn't offer the ancillary skills to buoy him at a constant floor of positive impact. He is also only 24, the same age as Warriors Rookie of the Year candidate Yaxel Lendeborg , so the Pelicans could see room to further develop him in their system. For the Suns, this would be a bet on their system. They have built a menacing defensive identity over the past two seasons and often punch above their weight through effort and hustle. Bringing Murray into this system could help to revive some of the defensive aspects of his game that have faded in recent years. Trade No. 2 Pelicans get: Four second-round picks Charlotte Hornets get: Murray In this unusual deal, the Pelicans get no players back. It is a valid trade because of the $40 million trade exception that the Hornets received in the LaMelo Ball trade. Four second-round picks may not sound like much, but in the process the Pelicans would also open up a $32 million trade exception of their own and would completely clear Murray's money off their books without receiving any undesirable contracts in return. The Hornets' offense has been really struggling this season, ranking last in Offensive Net Points per game, after losing their offensive engine in LaMelo Ball. Trading for Murray could inject some life into their offense, strengthening their guard play while they wait for Kon Knueppel to return from injury and Coby White to return to form after a slow start to his season. Trade No. 3 Pelicans get: De'Aaron Fox and Spurs 2029 first-round pick San Antonio Spurs get: Murray and Herb Jones The Pelicans here get a proven winner and veteran presence in Fox, who could help to mentor Jeremiah Fears and their other young players throughout their roster. They also receive a 2029 first-round pick to build their future draft capital. The Spurs are rolling right now and Fox has been playing great, so this would likely be a trade they consider only if things start to go downhill a bit and they decide they want to get off Fox's contract. San Antonio might be more interested in Murray than other teams, since he played some of his best basketball there. In this deal they also receive a very valuable player in Jones, whose defensive ability could slot perfectly into the Spurs' lineups and make the Victor Wembanyama -anchored defense even more impenetrable. -- Benjamin Tiemeyer Have any more ideas on what move the Pelicans should make involving Dejounte Murray? Like, is it Jarrett Allen ? Is it Sam Merrill ? I mean, Jaylon Tyson 's on a rookie contract here. Like, the only big trade chip left for them is Jarrett Allen." Latest episodes of the 'Hoop Collective' podcast Nov. 10 Brown last talked to Tatum in June to discuss future ESPN's Shams Charania reported that the last time Jaylen Brown and Jayson Tatum spoke was in June after the Boston Celtics failed to trade for Giannis Antetokounmpo . Brown confronted Tatum at a dinner in France about their future as teammates, per Charania. The former teammates will meet for the first time Tuesday night, as the Celtics head to Philadelphia (8 p.m. ET). NBA Trade Lab updates: How could the Lakers level up? The Los Angeles Lakers find themselves at the top of the Western Conference standings, with Luka Doncic playing like the best player in the world and leading the way in ESPN's Net Points Metric . Their projected win total from ESPN's Basketball Power Index that started the season at 45 has already increased to 53. They completely retooled their roster this past offseason after losing LeBron James in free agency to the Philadelphia 76ers , but their newly added pieces have jelled together quickly to leave fans around the league rethinking what the ceiling of this team could be. After sending out two first-round picks and two first-round pick swaps in the Walker Kessler sign-and-trade , the Lakers are very limited in remaining draft capital they could use to add another major piece through a trade. However, this hasn't stopped Lakers fans from diving into our NBA Trade Lab tool to cook up some mock trades in an attempt to find the Lakers another piece around the margins that could complete this roster for a deep playoff run. Trade No. 1: Lakers bring in Luka's former teammate Lakers get: P.J. Washington Dallas Mavericks get: Jarred Vanderbilt , Cameron Carr , and two second-round picks Washington is a versatile two-way wing who started alongside Doncic during the Mavericks' run to the finals in 2024. Washington played the best basketball of his career alongside Luka during their time together on the Mavs and would be a proven contributor to add to the Lakers' depth. Carr, the 24th overall pick in the 2026 draft, is a promising young player the Mavericks can plug in right away and develop around their young core. The two second-round picks would also be a welcome addition for Dallas, which currently doesn't have any second-round picks (outside of a top-55 protected Hawks' 2027 second-rounder). Trade No. 2: L.A. adds a big man Lakers get: Jalen Smith Chicago Bulls get: Jaden Hardy and two second-round picks Smith is a young intriguing stretch big, whose advanced metrics paint as a positive player even on a middling Bulls team. Despite averaging only 17 minutes a game in his career, Smith possesses a rare blend of rim defense, rebounding and 3-point shooting. This would be a buy-low opportunity for the Lakers to invest in the potential of Smith, letting him play off one of the best playmakers in the world in Luka Doncic . If the Bulls aren't as convinced about Smith's potential or are unsure of what kind of an extension they would give him this upcoming summer, they could decide to trade him before the deadline rather than lose him for nothing. Trade No. 3: Lakers get help on defense Lakers get: Derrick Jones Jr. LA Clippers get: Jaden Hardy and three second-round picks Jones is a talented defender who also started alongside Luka Doncic during the Mavericks' 2024 Finals run. He was an unsung hero throughout that 2024 playoff run as he held his own on defense against the likes of Shai Gilgeous-Alexander and Anthony Edwards . His thin frame combined with outlier athleticism allows him to navigate around screens and successfully shadow the shiftiest superstars in a way that few others in the league can. His addition to the Lakers as a reliable point-of-attack defender would be immensely helpful in slowing down an opposing star guard in a playoff series. The Clippers' future draft assets are severely depleted after the NBA stripped them of five future first-round picks for circumventing the salary cap. It makes sense for the Clippers to try to parlay any valuable veteran players on their current roster to start to recoup some future draft capital. Have any ideas on what move the Lakers should make? Build it in the NBA Trade Lab , then submit your trade to let fans vote on it from both sides. -- Ben Tiemeyer Nov. 9 NBA Trade Lab updates: The latest Sabonis deals As my colleague Ben Tiemeyer wrote earlier, Golden State Warriors center Kristaps Porzingis is the player most involved in fan-created trades in the new NBA Trade Lab. While Porzingis has the most interest, trading for Sacramento Kings center Domantas Sabonis could be the most impactful. The Kings sit in the bottom of the Western Conference standings and have prioritized building their roster with young players, notably lottery pick Darius Acuff Jr . They have gone from one of the oldest rosters in the NBA last season to a team with seven players 26 years old or younger this season. Sabonis was named All-NBA in 2024 and appeared in 82 games. However, last season he played the fewest games (19) in his career and had season ending knee surgery in February. Sabonis has two years and $94 million left on his contract ($45.5 and $48.6 million). Below are some of the top fan-created trades involving Sabonis, as scored by fans voting from the perspective of each team involved: Trade No. 1 Kings get: A top-4 protected first from a rebuilding Chicago is strong value for the Kings. The three final groups are Nancy Walton Laurie and Bill Laurie; Steve Apostolopoulos and Marc Lasry; Bill Foley and Jerry Colangelo, sources told ESPN. Will KAT take a pay cut in next Knicks deal? On "NBA Today," ESPN's Malika Andrews detailed Karl-Anthony Towns ' mindset toward contract negotiations with the defending champion New York Knicks . "Towns, from what I have been told, is willing -- similarly to what Jalen Brunson did [but the] numbers aren't the same -- to take a pay cut," Andrews said. "But the pay cut that the Knicks are asking him to take, he views as unreasonable." Towns, 30, is eligible to sign a four-year, $276 million extension through June 30. Embiid "full participant" in first Sixers' practice Joel Embiid was a "full participant all the way through" for the Philadelphia 76ers first practice of training camp, Sixers coach Nick Nurse said Tuesday. "He looked great," Nurse said of Embiid. "Very, very good news from the standpoint of where it's been the last couple years, last couple summers leading into today. ... It's great to see." After being named the league MVP in 2023, the 32-year-old center has missed 150 games over the last three seasons because of various injuries. He also sat out four of the Sixers' 11 playoff games in the spring because of appendicitis, right hip soreness and a right ankle sprain. The only Sixers player who did not participate in Tuesday's practice according to a team spokesperson was backup big man Adem Bona , who is dealing with a sprained left foot. Anfernee Simons , who signed a two-year, $12.3 million contract to join Philadelphia in July, said Embiid's presence in the gym was already notable leading up to the start of camp. "Everybody's been impressed around here about how he's come in and worked," Simons said. "Joel is going to be Joel. He's going to be a dominant player always. We just want to continue for him to be himself, as well, and I think everybody's going to be able to work around that." Despite the injuries, the 10-year veteran still averaged 26.9 points, 7.7 rebounds, 3.9 assists and 1.2 blocks per game last season. Embiid's inclusion only added to what several Sixers players described as an "exciting" opening day with LeBron James and Jaylen Brown completing their first official practice with the franchise. "With any team, we got to start somewhere, and then we got to get better and better, and just keep trying to reach our ceiling, right?" Nurse said. "That happens day-to-day. Can we get up tomorrow, like, 98% as excited as we did today? It's going to be hard to get as excited as we all were today, right? "But we need to come back, and we need to keep climbing that mountain. That's a daily process. I just want them to reach their potential. If they do, great things are going to happen." -- Dave McMenamin Hoop Collective: The 2026 NBA Media Day reaction special Brian Windhorst is joined by ESPN reporters from around the league to check in on Monday's Media Days. Tim MacMahon, Dave McMenamin, Vince Goodwill, Jamal Collier, Anthony Slater and Michael C. Wright all hop on the podcast to discuss the biggest storylines throughout the NBA ahead of training camp. Latest episodes of the 'Hoop Collective' podcast Top NBA media day headlines LeBron says he envisioned joining Knicks as free agent | Philly stars ready to 'sacrifice' Clippers apologize to fans, vow to move past investigation | Ingram (Achilles) out Edwards happy to cede Wolves' PG duties to Ball Wizards, AD to wait until summer for extension talks Karl-Anthony Towns wants extension to stay with Knicks Jokic on his next Nuggets deal: 'I'm going to sign next year' Bronny on LeBron James' Lakers exit: 'He's got his own path' Sept. 28 Bronny on LeBron James' Lakers exit: 'He's got his own path' When LeBron James chose to leave the Los Angeles Lakers in free agency over the summer, he consulted his family on the decision to sign with the Philadelphia 76ers . But when it came to his son/teammate Bronny, much was apparently left unsaid . "We're men of very little words when it comes to talking about business and what we're going to do and how we feel about each other. So it wasn't really much [discussion] to be honest with you," Bronny James said Monday at Lakers media day. "He's got his own path and I got my own. He knows that I want to make a name for myself and I want to continue my career and keep growing as a player. And he knows that I want to focus on that. So he decided to do that." LeBron and Bronny have routinely been in unique situations in league history, whether it was opening night two years ago, when the father and son entered the game together, or last year in the playoffs, where they combined to deliver a 10-0 run during a victory over the Houston Rockets . Navigating a complex free agency in which the father leaves and the son stays is another one for the books. Tatum 'comfortable' leading new-look Celtics post-Brown trade Jayson Tatum 's one constant during his development into a star with the Boston Celtics was having Jaylen Brown as a teammate. That partnership ended this offseason when the Celtics' front office decided to trade Brown -- the 2024 NBA Finals MVP -- to the Philadelphia 76ers in what was largely a cost-cutting move that broke up the duo most responsible for leading Boston to the 2024 NBA championship. "The business of the NBA comes and plays a part at some point. And I've seen it in my almost 10 years in this league," Tatum said during Celtics media day on Monday . "For me it's more so being grateful for what we accomplished and what he means for this city and to this organization. Just the ups and downs in our career that we were able to grow and learn from and made us the players that we are today. So really just being thankful for those nine years." Suns owner Ishbia says mortgage company woes won't hurt team It's well-known at this point that billionaire Mat Ishbia's mortgage company has had a rough financial stretch. The owner of the Phoenix Suns said Monday that will have "zero" effect on his spending habits when it comes to basketball. In fact, the 46-year-old said he's working on purchasing 14% more of the team, bringing his total to roughly 80%. Ishbia's company -- United Wholesale Mortgage -- suffered a reported $450 million net loss in the second quarter this year, calling into question if the sizable dip would affect his basketball business. The outspoken Ishbia was adamant that nothing would change for the NBA franchise when it comes to spending on players or the fan experience. Williamson not where he wants to be New Orleans Pelicans forward Zion Williamson kept his answer brief when asked how he would summarize his first seven years as an NBA player. "I'm not where I want to be," said Williamson, whom the Pelicans drafted with the No. 1 pick out of Duke in 2019. "I'm not where I need to be." Butler indicates he is 'ahead' in his knee rehab Nearing the eight-month mark since his right ACL surgery , Jimmy Butler III is hesitant to put a specific target date on his eventual NBA return, but he did express optimism in advance of Golden State Warriors training camp. "I promise you I'm coming back, and it's going to be -- I think it's going to be, like, real eye-popping for everybody how I'm still going to be nice," Butler said. "Probably nicer, honestly." Butler has only recently advanced to running, and he will be limited to light on-court individual work when the team begins practice in Hawaii on Tuesday afternoon. It will be several weeks before Butler is expected to advance to a more rigorous stage of his rehab, and the team's lead medical decision-maker, Rick Celebrini, is known for his cautiousness in the later stages of the rehab process. A January or February return can be considered on the optimistic side for Butler, who turned 37 earlier this month. But Butler did say that the strengthening tests on the knee indicate he is ahead of schedule. "My numbers are staggering," Butler said. "They're off the charts. I'm ahead, so they say. So, I just know that all the work that I've been doing, whether it be at home, in L.A., in Europe, in South America, wherever the case may be, I've been doing all the right things. So, I am confident that whenever I come back, I'll be more than ready, I'll be more than healthy and I'll be a better all-around player than I was whenever I went down." -- Anthony Slater Pistons eye "better version" of Cunningham Detroit Pistons coach J.B. Bickerstaff has held many offseason conversations with All-NBA guard Cade Cunningham about seizing greatness and the necessary steps toward improving after last year's playoff run that stretched to Game 7 of the Eastern Conference semifinals. Bickerstaff has guaranteed "a better version" Cunningham this season, which could be a scary sight after he averaged 23.9 points, 9.9 assists, 5.5 rebounds and 1.4 steals in 33.9 minutes during 2025-26. But Cunningham also led the East in turnovers per game after finishing with the second most in 2024-25. "I don't have to challenge Cade, and that's why he is who he is," Bickerstaff said. "Because he's pulling. He's not being pushed." Cunningham showed up in a fresh pair of Nike S.T. Charge "Detroit Tough" sneakers in Pistons colors. He will also receive his own signature Nike shoe, which is expected to debut during the second half of the season. "I'm thankful to be in these shoes. I'm thankful to have the opportunity to represent my family in this way," Cunningham said. "Represent where I come from, but then to represent the city of Detroit. "In a city like this, it's a blessing. I'm thankful for it, I don't take it for granted and I'm trying to make the most out of it." -- Eric Woodyard Hornets waive former No. 8 pick Dillingham The Charlotte Hornets are waiving guard Rob Dillingham , sources told ESPN's Shams Charania . Dillingham was traded from the Chicago Bulls on Saturday for Buddy Hield and cash. The Hornets created a $9.6 million trade exception with the move. Dillingham, 21, appeared in 30 games for the Bulls last season, averaging 9.6 points and 2.8 assists. SGA on chance at historic third straight MVP At Oklahoma City Thunder media day, guard Shai Gilgeous-Alexander discussed the possibility of winning a third straight NBA MVP award and whether that's something he ponders going into this season. "No different than any other year: Try to be the best player I can be, try to implement the things I just worked on," Gilgeous-Alexander said. "The decision for MVP is literally 82 games away. I'm not going to win the award in the first week of the season. ... That kind of recipe for me in the past has kind of worked, and I've been fortunate to win two in a row. "We need to be laser focused on ourselves. We need to take the lessons from that [Western Conference finals] series, for sure, and we did. But it's certainly not something that we overcorrect for, because you end up chasing your shadow, and it prevents you from being your best as you move forward." ESPN's Summer Forecast gave Gilgeous-Alexander the fourth-best chance at the 2027 MVP, behind Victor Wembanyama , Nikola Jokic and Luka Doncic . No player has won three consecutive MVPs since Larry Bird in 1984, 1985 and 1986. -- Baxter Holmes Doncic talks LeBron exit, Lakers "championship" ceiling Speaking to ESPN's Brian Windhorst during Los Angeles Lakers media day, guard Luka Doncic detailed his reaction to LeBron James leaving for the Philadelphia 76ers this past summer and why he thinks a successful 2026-27 includes a Lakers run to the title: "It was kind of sad. Playing with LeBron was amazing. There's a lot of things I learned from him. ... We all know who LeBron James is." Shams: Duren's relationship with Pistons "has fractures" Simmons "didn't touch a ball for a year" During Sacramento Kings media day, guard Ben Simmons laid out the reasons he chose the Kings and why he's excited for the 2026-27 season. "The expectations are low. I feel like that's been something on me too, so we can relate in that way," Simmons told reporters. "I think we have a chip on our shoulder." Simmons last played in 2024-25, appearing in 51 games for the Brooklyn Nets and LA Clippers . The three-time All-Star said the time away gave him the chance to focus on "getting my body right and my mind right." Pistons GM hasn't spoken with Duren all summer Jalen Duren and the Detroit Pistons have a decision to make as the clock ticks closer to Oct. 1 -- the deadline to sign a one-year, $9.6 million qualifying offer. For Duren, he can accept the five-year, $200 million contract that has been offered by Detroit or he can become the first player named All-NBA or All-Star to sign the qualifying offer. If he chooses the latter, Duren will hold veto power on any trade this season and be an unrestricted free agent next summer. For the Pistons, weighing the risk of having an All-NBA player on a one-year contract and, more importantly, the likelihood he will depart next summer as a free agent is key. There are eight projected teams that have significant cap space to sign Duren to a four-year, $189 million max contract. "I can't control the different things that he does or his group does," Pistons president of basketball operations Trajan Langdon said at media day. "For me, it's control what we can and letting him know he is a big part of what we do." Langdon also said he hasn't spoken with Duren all summer during Pistons media day. -- Bobby Marks Mitchell: LeBron to Cavs made sense "for a lot of reasons" At Cavaliers media day, Donovan Mitchell said that in his mind, he thought LeBron James would return to Cleveland because "for a lot of reasons it made sense." "I didn't think Philly. I thought if he didn't come here, it'd be Golden State," Mitchell said. After being swept in the Eastern Conference finals by the eventual champion New York Knicks then missing out on James in free agency, Cleveland kept its core intact. The Cavs signed Mitchell to a four-year, $273 million maximum extension and re-signed James Harden to a three-year, $97 million contract. Cleveland did make one major addition by acquiring Peyton Watson from the Denver Nuggets in a multiteam trade then signing the restricted free agent to a four-year, $88 million deal. Speaking for the first time since their extensions, Mitchell and Harden both said their approaches to their new deals -- Mitchell signing as soon as he was eligible with Harden opting out to give Cleveland more flexibility to make moves -- reflected a team-first mindset. "This is something that I want to do, and I want to win a championship," Harden said. "So, what does that look like? Making the team better, making the team whole to where we give ourselves a chance. By the way, you can have the best talented team, which I've been on before, and still not win. "We waited, waited, waited until the front office called me, made sure that we got everything that we can get, and then we signed. We got a long way to go, but I love the direction and steps that we're taking here as a unit from top to bottom." -- Daniel Oyefusi MacMahon: Thunder adjusting to roster changes The departures of three championship-winning teammates doesn't yet feel like reality for Thunder superstar Shai Gilgeous-Alexander , who kidded that he still expected Luguentz Dort , Isaiah Joe and Aaron Wiggins to show up for Oklahoma City's team picture Monday afternoon. "It's the business of the NBA, right?" Gilgeous-Alexander said, referring to the series of financially motivated trades. "I don't think anybody has played with all 12 guys their whole career. It sucks a little bit. "My mind never even went to what we were going to be like on the court. It was more like the brotherhood." As fellow OKC guard Jalen Williams added, "It's the weirdest thing ever." -- Tim MacMahon Clippers announce Ingram has partially torn Achilles The LA Clippers announced they found a partially torn Achilles tendon in Brandon Ingram 's foot after his recent heel surgery. He will miss the start of the 2026-27 season. Jokic: "I'm gonna sign next year" Denver Nuggets center Nikola Jokic reiterated his commitment to the franchise at Monday's media day. "I'm gonna sign next year," Jokic said. "If they want me." Curry said knee is ready to go for the season Golden State Warriors superstar guard Stephen Curry addressed the media Monday in offering positive updates on his injured knee. "Knee's feeling great. Ready to go. No issues," Curry said. "I feel a lot stronger and understanding of what I'm dealing with." Curry did acknowledge a "management element" but said there are currently no restrictions. Nuggets confident in Jokic's future with franchise Members of the Denver Nuggets ' front office, general manager Jon Wallace and executive vice president of basketball Ben Tenzer addressed the media on Monday and answered questions regarding Nikola Jokic 's future with the franchise. The three-time MVP didn't sign an extension this offseason. "We feel very comfortable with the relation and trust there," Tenzer said. "We have no concerns." LeBron: I wanted to finish my career with the Knicks New Philadelphia 76er LeBron James said his decision came down to five teams this offseason and that he envisioned going to the New York Knicks before they won the 2026 title. "I had visions of playing in [Madison Square] Garden and finishing my career in the Garden," James told ESPN on Monday during the 76ers' media day. "One of the best places I've ever played. "I think it's the No. 1 arena in the world, as far as for a basketball player. But after they beat San Antonio, I was like, 'Hey, I can't.' I couldn't do it." James and the 76ers will play the Knicks at the Garden on opening night, Oct. 20. No update on Gary Trent Jr. investigation Milwaukee Bucks governor Wes Edens did not provide an update on the league investigation into Gary Trent Jr. 's contract. "I don't have any update," Edens said. "We're working with the league and fully cooperating with them. But I don't have any insight beyond that." The NBA is looking into a potential cap-circumvention violation by the Bucks around Trent's deal this offseason. Cronin: Blazers have "belief" in Ja Morant Portland Trail Blazers ' general manager Joe Cronin addressed why the franchise decided to trade for Ja Morant this offseason during Portland's media day on Monday. "Just straight belief in Ja," Cronin said. "Our view of Ja as still a very high-level player. "I'm sure there will be questions about fit, but we're very focused on talent." Cronin also said veteran guard Jrue Holiday could play some minutes on the wing for Portland this season, while adding that Holiday and veteran guard Damian Lillard will have a positive influence on Morant. Kerr: Rookie Lendeborg going to "play a ton" Golden State Warriors coach Steve Kerr said during Monday's media day that he expects rookie Yaxel Lendeborg to "play a ton" this season. "He's clearly going to play a ton," Kerr said. "He gives us the size and the versatility that we need. "Whether he's a starter or coming off the bench, that will be determined the next couple of weeks." Lendeborg was the No. 11 pick in the 2026 NBA draft and averaged 15.1 points per game at Michigan last season. Embiid: 'Extremely excited' about this year's team Philadelphia 76ers center Joel Embiid said Monday that he feels like the team finally has the right mix of players, after an offseason in which the franchise traded for Jaylen Brown and signed LeBron James to join the young guard tandem of VJ Edgecombe and Tyrese Maxey . "It's hard to win when you get a group of guys together for one year, two years, maybe," he said. "I'm extremely excited about this team because we have the right mix of veteran leadership and younger guys. We might have some ups and downs, but we're gonna get there." Wembanyama addresses last year's Finals loss After leading by double digits in each of the five games in last season's NBA Finals, San Antonio Spurs center Victor Wembanyama said his memories of it will fuel the team this season. "I couldn't imagine a better motivation," he said. Harper addresses role for coming season After offseason chatter about his role, San Antonio Spurs guard Dylan Harper said he'd follow the coaches' lead this season. "Everyone has a competitive edge to them. But the biggest thing for me is whatever I can do, just like last year, to help the team win," he said. "Whatever position the coaches think is best for me to be in, that's the position I'll happily go in." First look at LeBron in a 76ers uniform New Philadelphia 76ers forward LeBron James is taking questions from reporters on Monday. Here's what he had to say when asked about his initial impressions of his team: "Everybody is on the same page," James said. "We are all speaking the same language." LeBron addressed his role too, saying he's open to whatever the team needs from him to win. "Whatever they need me to do," he said. "The luxury of my game is I can do everything. ... Literally, I can do everything" Kawhi: I was a distraction, ready to move forward In his first public appearance with the Toronto Raptors after a controversy-filled summer, Kawhi Leonard addressed the NBA's investigation into him and his business dealings. "I know why some of you guys came. You want to hear about the investigation. But in talking with the NBA and PA, I think the best decision is to move forward and focus on my time being a Toronto Raptor," he said. "I already was a distraction for the past 70 days and wasn't able to meet my teammates or do any of that stuff, minicamp stuff, so, moving forward, I just want to talk about the Toronto Raptors." Haliburton: I am 100% healthy Indiana Pacers guard Tyrese Haliburton said Monday that he is healthy and ready for the season. "I am healthy. I am 100%," he said. "There will be no restrictions. That is not news. There is no source. I am the source. I am ready to go for the year." Porzingis out indefinitely in blow to Warriors Golden State Warriors big man Kristaps Porzingis is out indefinitely to open training camp with a health issue, according to the team. In late July, Porzingis agreed to a two-year, $40 million contract with a player option on the second season to return to the Warriors. Brown: KAT, Hart extension talks won't be a distraction After reports surfaced last week that negotiations between the New York Knicks and center Karl-Anthony Towns had hit a stalemate, coach Mike Brown said Monday neither Towns' situation nor Hart's would linger in the locker room. "We talk about everything [with the team]," Brown said. "We don't want to have any elephants in the room." "I'm not involved in it. They'll figure it out. Control what you can control." And here's what Towns said about a potential extension: "I've made it known I want to play here. Been a fan since I was a kid. I'd like to get it done." Hornets GM: Brandon Miller to be ready for training camp After undergoing offseason surgery on his left shoulder, Hornets wing Brandon Miller should be a full participant in training camp and "ready to roll" for opening night, Hornets general manager Jeff Peterson said Monday. Miller, 23, is entering his fourth NBA season after being the No. 2 pick in the 2023 draft. Duren won't be at Pistons media day, start of camp Detroit Pistons All-Star center Jalen Duren is not attending the team's media day on Monday or the start of training camp as his contract standoff continues, sources told ESPN's Shams Charania on Monday. Duren, a restricted free agent, is declining the team's five-year, $200 million fully guaranteed offer as both sides remain at a stalemate ahead of the Thursday deadline on a one-year, $9.6 million qualifying offer, sources said. Sept. 26 Bulls trade Dillingham to Hornets for Hield, cash The Chicago Bulls and Charlotte Hornets agreed to a trade sending Rob Dillingham to Charlotte for Buddy Hield and cash, the teams announced Saturday. 2026 NBA offseason trade grades Sept. 25 What's next for Curry and the Warriors? Stephen Curry 's two-year, $116 million extension made him the first player in NBA history to amass $600 million in career on-court earnings. The deal has also put the Golden State Warriors in position to have extra spending power next summer. By Curry taking $10 million less than the maximum allowed, the Warriors project to have nearly $38 million in cap space in 2027. Golden State could increase its projection to $55 million if center Kristaps Porzingis is waived in the offseason. Porzingis' $20 million salary for next season is guaranteed for $3 million. For Golden State to have ample room, forwards Draymond Green and Jimmy Butler III would need to sign elsewhere or at a significantly lesser salary. They will be free agents next summer. Both salary projections include the $17 million free agent hold of guard Brandin Podziemski . The 2023 first-round pick is eligible until Oct. 19 to extend his contract. -- Bobby Marks Grading the Curry deal: Why Warriors don't get an A Hornets star Knueppel sidelined by hamstring injury The Charlotte Hornets announced that Kon Knueppel will be out for at least the entire preseason because of a left hamstring injury. James: Maxey, Embiid were factors in joining 76ers LeBron James said his longstanding friendship with All-Star Tyrese Maxey and a desire to help Joel Embiid win his first NBA title played significant roles in his decision to sign a two-year, $8 million contract with the Philadelphia 76ers in July. "[Embiid has] done everything in our league, and the only thing he has not done is win a championship. And I want to try to help him get that first one," James said. "He has a city on his back. He's been 'The Process' for 10 years, 12 years, however long he's been there. But I think it's time we even get you deeper into the process. And I hope that I can be, kind of, that final little piece that can help him get over the hump." Grizzlies waive Russell The Memphis Grizzlies have waived D'Angelo Russell , sources told ESPN's Shams Charania. Russell has made one All-Star team during his career and was selected No. 2 in the 2015 NBA draft.

(Photo by Sarah Stier/Getty Images) | Getty Images An impressive performance for Jaylen Brown on Monday night ended in a late exit from the contest due to hamstring tightness, Nick Nurse confirmed to reporters postgame after the Sixers’ win over the Nets. Now, Brown has been ruled out for Philadelphia’s Wednesday game against the Orlando Magic, listed officially with a left hamstring strain. Monday night had been a great one for Brown up to his exit — minus bonking heads with Julius Randle early in the fourth and ending up with a forehead cut, from which he returned to the contest. Brown tied his season-high with 31 points and grabbed a season-high 13 rebounds in the Sixers’ victory. There was no clear moment on the broadcast of the game that showed when Brown may have suffered the injury. Jaylen Brown ties his season high with 31 points vs. Nets, posting a double-double with 13 rebounds all in 33 minutes. 31 PTS, 13 REB, 4 AST, 1 STL, 1 BLK. Here's every field goal from Brown tonight 🔽 pic.twitter.com/nGhYfSUm5b — Erin Grugan (@eringrugan) November 17, 2026 Brown has been extremely durable across his career. Excluding the two NBA seasons shortened by COVID, 63 games played is the fewest total for him since he entered the league. He’s gotten this season off to a great start with his new squad, averaging 22.6 points shooting 38.6% from long range with 6.6 rebounds, 3.6 assists and 1.3 steals per contest. The best case scenario here would be that the Sixers are being extra cautious with Brown, especially so early in the season and against a weaker opponent like the Magic. After Wednesday night’s game, the Sixers will get few full days off before returning to action on Saturday afternoon hosting the Milwaukee Bucks, so Brown will get at least three days off here. Hopefully the injury is minor and he is able to play again soon.
