stories.title: NBA trade rumors 2026-27: Dejounte Murray market lukewarm, what about Zion Williamson?
stories.summary: While Murray would like a trade sooner rather than later, expect this process to drag out.
stories.detailText: Nov 8, 2026; Inglewood, California, USA; New Orleans Pelicans guard Dejounte Murray (5) dribbles the ball during the third quarter against the Los Angeles Clippers at Intuit Dome. Mandatory Credit: Kiyoshi Mio-Imagn Images IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect NBA front offices generally wait about 20 games to assess their teams before seriously looking into the trade market. Even more, it's not until Dec. 15, when many contracts signed over the summer become trade-eligible, that the market really heats up. That, however, never stops the NBA trade rumor mill, so here is the latest. Tepid Dejounte Murray market Soon after news broke of Dejounte Murray's agent requesting a trade for the point guard out of New Orleans, rumors tried to link Murray to the Phoenix Suns. There was some logic to it: The salaries line up and, at least outside the Valley of the Sun, the sense is Phoenix could use a point guard. However, most of that speculation seemed to come out of Murray's camp, not Phoenix, which has limited interest in him, according to multiple reports, including Chris Manix here at NBC Sports. He also reports the market for Murray is "lukewarm." Actually, lukewarm may be putting it kindly. Here is what one "high ranking" NBA executive told Kelly Iko of Yahoo Sports : "What a f****** mess. No one wants to touch him." Coming off a torn Achilles that cost him most of two seasons, other teams see Murray as a distressed asset making $32.8 million this season, with a player option he almost certainly picks up for $30.8 million next season. Teams will want picks, likely a first-round pick, to take on that much money. Based on the history of Pelicans lead executive Joe Dumars in dealing with Trey Murphy III and Herb Jones (two players other teams actually want), this is going to drag out. Doug Christie on hot seat? The Sacramento Kings are 1-12 and their coach, Doug Christie, is in the final year of his contract. On 29 teams in the league, that would be the definition of a coach on the hot seat, but in Sacramento they pushed back hard when the idea first came out, saying Christie was safe. He is a favorite of ownership there. That hasn't completely changed. Marc Stein of The Stein Line reports the Kings "would prefer not to fire" Christie during the season to limit the amount of "tumult and upheaval" during Darius Acuff Jr.'s rookie campaign. Most likely, Christie is let go after the season. If/when that happens, two names to watch are Tom Thibodeau and Mark Jackson. Thibodeau (who has connections to GM Scott Perry) has coached more recently and had more success, while former Warriors coach Mark Jackson is a favorite of owner Vivek Ranadive from those days in Golden State. In other Sacramento news, they are still interested in adding veteran point guard Gabe Vincent as a backup behind Acuff, he has a standing offer, Stein reports. That he hasn't jumped at the deal could be telling. Other trade rumors • With all the Pelicans trade talk right now, would they consider trading Zion Williamson? Maybe, but the return isn't going to be as robust as they might hope, reports ESPN’s Tim MacMahon on the Hoop Collective podcast : "He's somewhere on the LaMelo (Ball) to Ja (Morant) spectrum, in terms of trade value." Ball went for a first-round pick and Naz Reid, plus three pick swaps, and MacMahon is saying Williamson would get a smaller return than that. Morant was traded for Jerami Grant and Kris Murray. • While the Miami Heat have found a groove of late, this is a team known to be looking for upgrades, and Ira Winderman of the Sun Sentinel suggests to watch out for Zach LaVine as a target. “I would keep an eye on that name” Amid their five-game winning streak, @IraHeatBeat suggests how Zach LaVine could be a nice addition to Miami’s roster with @TheFrankIsola & @Scalabrine FULL SHOW HERE: https://t.co/XvyIdd1Wfp pic.twitter.com/w1t36U1cOy — SiriusXM NBA Radio (@SiriusXMNBA) November 17, 2026 • The Indiana Pacers may be in the market to trade for a wing, but they want to get Tyrese Haliburton back healthy and let things shake out first, Stein reports.

stories.title: Hawks lose guard CJ McCollum for at least 4 weeks with calf strain
stories.summary: Atlanta Hawks guard CJ McCollum will miss at least four weeks with a left calf strain, the team announced Tuesday.
stories.detailText: Atlanta Hawks guard CJ McCollum will miss at least four weeks with a left calf strain, the team announced Tuesday. McCollum hurt his leg in Sunday's win over the Milwaukee Bucks , although it was unclear when the injury occurred. He scored 20 points in 30 minutes for Atlanta in the win and was able to finish the game. However, following imaging, the Hawks diagnosed the veteran guard with a calf strain. He will be reevaluated after four weeks, the team said. Atlanta also lost forward Asa Newell for four months after further evaluation of his hyperextended left big toe revealed a plantar plate tear. He had surgery in New York on Tuesday. Newell, a first-round pick in the 2025 NBA draft, has been sidelined since Nov. 4 and appeared in just five games so far this season. McCollum, 35, is in his second season in Atlanta and is averaging 14.5 points in 26.4 minutes per game.

stories.title: Inside Sixers-Nets: How Philly can finish a back-to-back sweep in Brooklyn
stories.summary: Brooklyn reworked its roster around Julius Randle and Michael Porter Jr. but enters Monday at 3-9 as Philadelphia tries to win twice in two nights.
stories.detailText: Inside Sixers-Nets: How Philly can finish a back-to-back sweep in Brooklyn originally appeared on NBC Sports Philadelphia The Sixers will arrive in Brooklyn with one victory already secured on their back-to-back and a different combination of stars likely available for the second. Philadelphia improved to 11-3 with a 131-124 win over the Pacers on Sunday. Jaylen Brown scored a season-high 31 points, Tyrese Maxey added 27 and LeBron James recorded 11 assists to move past Jason Kidd for third in NBA history . James has not played both ends of a back-to-back this season, making it reasonable to expect him to sit Monday night. Joel Embiid, meanwhile, rested Sunday and is expected to return against Brooklyn. The Sixers had not submitted their official injury report as of Monday morning. The Nets enter at 3-9, but this is not the same roster that finished 20-62 last season. Before the Sixers attempt to win twice in two nights, here is a closer look at what has changed in Brooklyn and where Monday’s matchup could turn. Brooklyn changed its roster, not its early results Nic Claxton is now in Chicago. Julius Randle arrived from Minnesota as the central piece of a four-team trade. Keon Ellis and Moe Wagner joined in free agency, while Michael Porter Jr. remains one of Brooklyn’s primary scoring options. Porter is available after missing Saturday’s game for personal reasons. He will give the Nets another shooter after Brooklyn struggled badly without him in a 129-110 loss to Memphis. The Nets’ rotation also includes a large group of young players. Egor Dëmin, Nolan Traore and Mikel Brown Jr. have all received minutes in the backcourt, while Noah Clowney, Danny Wolf and Day’Ron Sharpe have played in the frontcourt. The combination has produced uneven results. Brooklyn averages 110.2 points and allows 116.4 per game. Its minus-6.3 net rating ranks 23rd in the league. Brooklyn has shown its offensive ceiling. The Nets scored 145 points in a 34-point win over New Orleans last week. Three nights later, they fell behind Memphis by 26 and lost by 19. Jordi Fernandez has been direct about the difference between the team he sees in practice and the one that has appeared in games. “We practice better than we play,” the Nets head coach said after Saturday’s loss . “It’s a frustrating sign because you believe you’re better.” Trying to establish order The Nets did not merely miss shots against Memphis. Their problems began with their approach. “We didn’t punch first,” Randle said. “Just organization. I think maybe just trying too hard, playing a little unorganized, stuff like that. And then just attention to detail. I think we’ve got a lapse of focus sometimes.” Fernandez was even more direct when discussing his young guards. “They’ve got to grow fast,” he said. “Being 20 is not an excuse.” That inexperience has appeared in Brooklyn’s ball control. The Nets’ offensive turnover rate ranks 28th in the league. They have been much more disruptive on the other end. Brooklyn has forced turnovers on 13.9 percent of its opponents’ possessions, tied for seventh. The Sixers forced 10 Indiana turnovers and converted them into 19 points Sunday. Philadelphia committed 13 total turnovers while playing at the quick tempo it has emphasized since training camp. Brooklyn has enough length and athleticism to disrupt the Sixers. It has not consistently maintained its own organization after creating that pressure. Philadelphia’s shooters have an opening Brooklyn has allowed 14.2 three-pointers per game, the eighth-most in the NBA. Opponents have posted a 55.2 effective field-goal percentage against the Nets. That presents another opportunity for a Sixers team receiving strong outside shooting from several role players. Anfernee Simons ranks third in the league with 33 three-pointers off the bench and is shooting 41.8 percent from deep. Kentavious Caldwell-Pope has made 46.5 percent of his threes, while Dean Wade is at 41.4 percent. Maxey made five threes against Indiana and Brown added three. Jabari Walker also continued his strong start by making three of his six attempts from deep. Those contributions matter on the second night of a back-to-back, especially if James sits. Philadelphia should not need Maxey and Brown to create every possession from a standstill if its shooters continue punishing open space. A different frontcourt matchup Embiid’s expected return would change the shape of Philadelphia’s offense after James served as its primary organizer Sunday. Brooklyn no longer has Claxton to use against Embiid. Sharpe has moved into a larger role and is coming off 16 points and 11 rebounds in Memphis. Wagner, Clowney and Randle give Fernandez several other bodies to try, but none presents the same defensive profile as Claxton. Sharpe’s work on the glass deserves attention. The Sixers have survived significant rebounding deficits this season, but allowing Brooklyn extra possessions would give Porter and Randle more chances to settle into the game. On the other end, Embiid should have opportunities to force Brooklyn’s frontcourt into difficult decisions. Sending help would create openings for Philadelphia’s shooters. Defending him individually would leave Sharpe, Wagner and Clowney with a demanding assignment. The Sixers have already won three games without James. Monday could require them to do it again, this time with Embiid returning as the center of the offense. Brooklyn’s record suggests a favorable matchup. Its shooting and young talent make it less comfortable than the standings indicate. The Sixers handled the first half of their back-to-back by producing a season-high 131 points. Finishing the sweep will require them to adjust to a different available roster while preventing an inconsistent Nets team from finding one of its explosive nights.

stories.title: Observations after Brown-Maxey duo scores 58 points in Sixers' win without Embiid
stories.summary: The Sixers improved to 11-3 on Sunday by beating the Pacers without Joel Embiid.
stories.detailText: Observations after Brown-Maxey duo scores 58 points in Sixers' win without Embiid originally appeared on NBC Sports Philadelphia The Jaylen Brown-Tyrese Maxey duo starred, LeBron James reached another milestone, and the Sixers earned a win without Joel Embiid on Sunday afternoon. They improved to 11-3 on the season with a 131-124 victory over the Pacers at Xfinity Mobile Arena. Brown scored 31 points and Maxey posted 27. LeBron James had 15 points and 11 assists. He passed Jason Kidd on Sunday for third in NBA history with 12,092 assists . Pascal Siakam scored 31 points for the 5-9 Pacers. On the first day of a back-to-back, the Sixers were down Embiid (right foot plantar fascia injury management), Dominick Barlow (lower back stress reaction) , Adem Bona (cervical spine sprain) and Ariel Hukporti (right Achilles tendon tear). The Pacers’ injured players included Tyrese Haliburton and Andrew Nembhard. The Sixers will face the Nets on Monday night in Brooklyn. Here are observations on their win over the Pacers: Walker’s 1st start Jabari Walker started for the first time this season, opening the game at center. He’s been in the Sixers’ rotation the past five games since Bona’s injury. Walker set up the Sixers’ first basket, swiping a steal and then tossing the ball ahead to Maxey for a fast-break dunk. Maxey and Brown both began well and combined to score all of the Sixers’ first 15 points. Though he conceded five inches to 7-foot Pacers center Ivica Zubac, Walker was solid in his first stint. He got an early post stop on Zubac and then snatched a strong defensive rebound. Dean Wade was next up for the Sixers at the five. He sunk a three-pointer on his first shot to give the team a 20-16 lead. Walker ended up playing 25 minutes and posting 11 points and seven rebounds. Going back to the preseason, his stock has steadily risen. “Here we are again after another game saying Jabari played very well,” Sixers head coach Nick Nurse said. “He plays hard, he rebounds, he’s got another level of confidence with his shooting this year. “It’s kind of wash, rinse and repeat again with him (today). He was great. … Jabari went in there and battled (Zubac). I thought he certainly matched him, if not outplayed him, which is a heck of a job.” Wade had 12 points and seven boards in 35 minutes. Overall, the Sixers’ lack of healthy conventional centers is still a clear deficiency. Of course, everything should be simpler once Embiid is back in action. An NBA chance for Philon The Sixers’ defense did not have a sparkling start. The Pacers tallied 35 points in the first quarter and shot 62.5 percent from the field. Brown helped the Sixers avoid a substantial deficit by draining all sorts of jumpers. He rarely appears bothered by close contests. Brown moved to 7 for 9 from the floor when he knocked down a three early in the second quarter. Kentavious Caldwell-Pope’s triple knotted the contest up at 37-all. Nurse needed to stray from his Plan A rotation when VJ Edgecombe picked up his third foul with 9:56 left in the second quarter. Labaron Philon Jr., who got a game with the G League’s Delaware Blue Coats on Friday night , subbed in. For a rookie guard , Philon has looked comfortable and confident on offense in most of his NBA appearances. He swished a long-range jumper in the second quarter and saw a floater rim out. Tacko time Brown reached the 20-point mark and put the Sixers up one with a slam assisted by James late in the second quarter. He ran into serious foul trouble in the third quarter. Brown was whistled for his fourth foul with 9:53 left in the period for an off-arm shove on Aaron Nesmith. Wade entered and Brown exited. The Sixers’ slim lead didn’t slip away. Walker nailed threes on consecutive possessions and Maxey jammed in a dunk. Soon after, Tacko Fall came in for his first meaningful minutes as a Sixer. The 7-foot-6 two-way contract player grabbed an offensive board off a missed Edgecombe free throw, which drew one of the day’s loudest cheers. With Fall on the floor, Maxey and James connected on an alley-oop that extended the Sixers’ lead to 82-73. When the Sixers tried to sit in a zone, Fall was called for a defensive three-second violation. Whatever the scheme, most of Fall’s defensive work will come around the paint. He certainly has exceptional physical traits as a rim protector and is not nimble on the perimeter. Fall logged five scoreless third-quarter minutes and recorded three rebounds. The Sixers outscored Indiana by a point with Fall on the court. Given Fall is occupying a (two-way) roster slot and the Sixers are so depleted at center, it made sense to see a bit of what he can do outside of garbage time. While five minutes isn’t enough for any grand conclusions, it’s very safe to say Fall is a unique player. “I’m 7-6, so I can change the game in so many ways,“ Fall said. “Offensively, setting screens, making sure guys get open, being an easy target for lobs. Defensively, I feel like I’ve always been an elite rim protector and I’ve worked on my body a lot to be able to move a lot better.” Nurse praised Fall’s outing, saying he “gave us some great minutes and a nice lift.” Fall is appreciative of his first NBA opportunity since the 2021-22 season. “I’ve worked very hard,” he said. “God has brought me back here and I’m thankful. And I’m ready. Whenever my name is called, I’m going to go out there and do my job.” The Sixers built their advantage to 102-87 with a Brown three early in the fourth quarter. They couldn’t cruise to a blowout, though. Siakam kept hurting the Sixers as a driver and had a highly efficient fourth quarter, scoring 19 points on 7-for-9 shooting. Quenton Jackson’s layup trimmed Indiana’s deficit to 119-115. The Sixers ultimately held off the Pacers’ push. Caldwell-Pope canned a three, Wade threw down an and-one dunk, and James checked off his milestone assist with a late dish to Edgecombe for a layup.

stories.title: ‘Hard to win': Simons, Walker carry Portland lessons into Sixers roles
stories.summary: Former Blazers teammates are contributing in different ways for a Sixers team built to contend.
stories.detailText: ‘Hard to win': Simons, Walker carry Portland lessons into Sixers roles originally appeared on NBC Sports Philadelphia Anfernee Simons and Jabari Walker shared the floor for 128 games in Portland. The Trail Blazers won 43 of them. They sat beside one another in the Sixers’ interview room Thursday night after a victory and discussed what the other 85 taught them. “Whether you’ve got a big role or a small role, it’s hard to win in the NBA,” Simons said. “We’ve seen it firsthand.” Their roles were considerably different then. Simons was an established starter entrusted with creating and scoring. Walker, a 2022 second-round pick, was trying to establish himself in a rotation. During their three overlapping seasons, Portland went 33-49, 21-61 and 36-46. The Blazers missed the playoffs each year. Both are now reserves on a Sixers team constructed to contend. In nine games they’ve both appeared in this season, Philadelphia is 7-2. They provided 26 points, 11 rebounds and six three-pointers in the Sixers’ 123-112 win over the Raptors at Xfinity Mobile Arena. Simons scored 17 points and shot 5 for 6 from three-point range. Walker recorded nine points and eight rebounds, including four on the offensive glass. The Sixers outscored Toronto by 24 points during Simons’ 23 minutes. Neither former Blazer committed a turnover. Their production helped Philadelphia overcome a 17-point first-quarter deficit and improve to 10-3 without LeBron James. “You learn once you come off the bench to kind of read the game before you get in there,” Simons said. “Obviously, we started off kind of slow. You just want to go in, bring some energy, get some stops, get out and run. I think everybody who got off the bench brought energy.” Simons supplied an immediate lift with a deep three-pointer at the first-quarter buzzer. His shot ended an 8-0 Sixers run and trimmed Toronto’s lead to nine. He remained involved during an 11-0 burst late in the third quarter, knocking down a three and setting up Walker for a basket. Walker then made a three early in the fourth before Simons scored on the Sixers’ next possession. When Toronto pulled within six with less than five minutes remaining, Simons answered with his fifth three-pointer. Making those shots is the most obvious way Simons can help a roster already featuring James, Joel Embiid, Tyrese Maxey and Jaylen Brown. He said the Sixers have not made him feel as though every opportunity must go in. “They encourage us to keep shooting the ball,” Simons said. “Knowing that a team has that much confidence in us to keep shooting makes the game that much easier. Whether you miss or make, as long as we get the right shots in the right moments, I think everybody can live with the misses and makes.” Simons spent seven seasons in Portland before playing last year with Boston and Chicago. His move to Philadelphia reunited him with Walker and Rayan Rupert, another former Blazer who joined the Sixers on a two-way contract during the offseason. Knowing familiar faces awaited him helped Simons enter another new locker room. “It made the transition seamless,” he said. “Just being able to have some comfortability with guys that I played with for multiple years. It’s been fun, kind of feeling like a little bit of old times. Me, Bari and Rups have been through a lot.” Walker’s path to Philadelphia began a year earlier and required an additional step. After playing 188 games over three seasons with Portland, Walker signed a two-way contract with the Sixers in July 2025. He earned a standard contract in February and has since pushed his way into the backup-center conversation despite standing 6-foot-7. Walker believes some of the work he did on losing teams was easily missed. “When I first got to the league, I was part of a rebuilding process,” he said. “I just felt like some of the little things I did didn’t always get noticed when you’re losing. I told myself, if I ever got to be part of a winning organization, then I’d go out and expand my abilities.” Rebounding has made Walker difficult for Nick Nurse to overlook. Walker credited his timing and strong hands to lessons passed down by his father, former NBA center Samaki Walker. Those instincts have become especially useful while the Sixers piece together their frontcourt behind Embiid. “Rebounding is a skill I kind of honed in on,” Walker said. “My dad was a good rebounder. He was known for his rebounding and his timing. I think it’s just a gift that he transferred to me.” Walker has made it clear that he expected to earn a role this season. “I don’t know if I was delusional, but I always felt like I was going to play and I was going to be a part,” he said. “I read something where they said it’s a surprise, but if you were around me this summer, it wouldn’t be a surprise. This is expected, and I just want to continue to get better.” The freedom Simons once had in Portland is no longer necessary. Walker does not need a high volume of touches, either. Both understand that playing beside the Sixers’ stars requires shooting when open, moving the ball and handling the less glamorous work. “You’ve got to find ways to impact the game multiple ways, even if you’re not scoring,” Simons said. “Whether it’s cutting, making the right read and pass to Joel, being the right swing pass to VJ, boxing out on defense or just being in the right position.” Their opportunities will fluctuate. Simons may take nine shots one night and only a few the next. Walker’s minutes will depend on matchups and the health of Philadelphia’s frontcourt. Winning has changed what they are being asked to do. Their three years together in Portland taught them why the adjustment is worthwhile. “You feel appreciative of the times where you go into a situation where your role might be a little bit less, but you’re winning,” Simons said. “That’s something you can’t take for granted.”

stories.title: Observations after Embiid posts season-high 37 points in Sixers' win over Nets
stories.summary: Joel Embiid’s season-best 37 points led the Sixers to victory on Monday night.
stories.detailText: Observations after Embiid posts season-high 37 points in Sixers' win over Nets originally appeared on NBC Sports Philadelphia Joel Embiid’s season-best 37 points led the Sixers to victory on Monday night in Brooklyn. The Sixers notched a 135-123 win over the Nets to move to 12-3 on the season. Brooklyn fell to 3-10. Jaylen Brown tied his season high with 31 points and set a new season high with 13 rebounds. Tyrese Maxey had 24 points and nine assists. Julius Randle’s 33 points topped the Nets. On the second night of a back-to-back, the Sixers were without LeBron James (lower back/sciatica management), Dominick Barlow (lower back stress reaction), Adem Bona (cervical spine sprain) and Ariel Hukporti (right Achilles tendon tear). The Sixers are now 4-0 without James. They’ll visit the Magic on Wednesday night. Here are observations on the Sixers’ win against the Nets: Sixers’ offense revolves around Embiid in first quarter Embiid returned after missing Sunday’s victory against the Pacers with the “right foot plantar fascia injury management” injury designation that’s become the norm for him early this season. He had an especially aggressive start in New York and set plenty of middle ball screens for Maxey. When the Nets blitzed or hard hedged Maxey, Embiid found a nice soft spot around the foul line and wasn’t hesitant to fire open jumpers. The 32-year-old big man posted 13 points in the first quarter on 6-for-11 shooting (1 for 2 from three-point range). Beyond the stats, it must be encouraging for the Sixers to watch Embiid trust his instincts and jumper. We’ll see whether he can sustain a good run and fully snap out of his shooting slump. Maxey broke the scoring ice when he swiped a steal and then coasted in for a dunk. Dean Wade’s put-back dunk gave the Sixers a 4-0 lead. Wade started in James’ place for the fourth time and had eight points and 11 rebounds over 32 minutes. With James out and Embiid back, Jabari Walker played at both power forward and center. He logged 16 minutes, a number that would’ve been higher without his foul trouble. Walker scored 12 points and grabbed five rebounds, the latest in a string of strong performances. Effective eight-man rotation The Sixers extended their lead at the start of the second quarter. Anfernee Simons drilled a corner three. The Sixers’ three-man bench shot 6 for 9 from the floor in the first half. Everyone who played for the Sixers chipped in something positive. Wade leapt up to snag a Walker miss and threw down an and-one dunk. VJ Edgecombe hit a floater to grow the Sixers’ advantage to 50-30. Embiid had a well-worn path to the foul line in the second quarter and made 9 of his 10 free throws. Sixers head coach Nick Nurse kept an eight-man rotation, only playing Simons, Walker and Kentavious Caldwell-Pope off the bench until the final 18.5 seconds. Sixers see it through after poor third quarter The Sixers’ collective effort on the glass was a major strength in the first half. All of the starters besides Maxey recorded at least one offensive rebound. Brown had a double-double before halftime and poured in 19 points over the first two quarters. The Sixers’ focus and intensity slipped in the third quarter. Nolan Traore’s layup cut Brooklyn’s deficit to single digits. Michael Porter Jr. hit a long two over Caldwell-Pope to trim the Sixers’ lead to six points. The Sixers concluded the third period on a high note. Walker sunk a buzzer-beating three to lift his team to a 105-95 edge. Again, the 24-year-old provided much more than intangible energy and made meaningful, momentum-shifting plays. The action stopped with 9:02 left in the fourth quarter after Brown was fouled by Randle. The Sixers’ star forward appeared to have his forehead collide with Randle’s face. He was down for several minutes before going to the bench. Randle needed stitches in his mouth before re-entering with 5:01 to go, Amy Fadool reported on the NBC Sports Philadelphia broadcast. Brown subbed back in with 6:02 remaining and a bandage on the cut above his left eye. However, he exited at the 1:44 mark and did not return. Nurse told reporters in Brooklyn that Brown was out at the end of the game because of “tightness,” according to PhillyVoice’s Adam Aaronson. After their shaky third quarter, the Sixers were ultimately fine in the fourth and reached a dozen wins. Egor Demin’s jumper pulled the Nets to within 125-121, but Embiid then iced the game by swishing a corner three.

stories.title: How LeBron James dissected Pacers defense down the stretch
stories.summary: James might not be the elite bucket-getter he once was, but he can still conduct highly-efficient offense.
stories.detailText: How LeBron James dissected Pacers defense down the stretch originally appeared on NBC Sports Philadelphia As he overtook Jason Kidd for the third-most assists in NBA history , LeBron James piloted the Sixers’ offense down the stretch against the Indiana Pacers on Sunday. With Joel Embiid sitting out and Tyrese Maxey getting a breather on the bench, James took over in the fourth quarter. He did so by spamming the same action over and over again. The set consisted of James getting a ball screen from a guard – either VJ Edgecombe or Anfernee Simons – at the top of the key. After setting or ghosting the screen, the guard would short roll towards the basket. When the Pacers blitzed or hedged the screen, James found the guard. The Sixers could then attack a 4-on-3 or 3-on-2 situation. Twice, Edgecombe and Simons scored off the roll. When the Pacers helped to the roller, that opened up the shooters in each corner. James directed traffic on offense to ensure that the Sixers spaced the floor properly. Here, he waved Dean Wade out of the dunker spot and into the corner. Edgecombe promptly hit him for an open three off the short roll. After all of the Sixers’ success, the Pacers eventually switched the ball screen. That left the 6-foot-4, 173-pound Quenton Jackson on James, who has five inches and 77 pounds on him. Jackson and James had already gone head to head on Sunday. In the first quarter, James set a ball screen for Edgecombe which the Pacers switched. Edgecombe fed James in the post and the Pacers doubled him to support Jackson. James punished them for it. They didn’t double James after the switch in the fourth quarter. This time, James backed Jackson down, backed him down again and backed him down some more before scoring inside. James’ strength abusing matchups against smaller defenders after switches has been a safety valve for the Sixers’ offense. Guards struggle to stop him from getting to the basket. When defenses send help, he picks them apart with his otherworldly passing ability. That combination forced the Pacers to pick their poison. From the 9:55 mark in the fourth until the Pacers switched to a zone defense (after James bullied Jackson) with just over 6:00 left, the Sixers scored 13 points out of this action across seven possessions. That’s a stellar 1.86 points per possession. James, who’s scoring a career-low 15.1 points per game so far this season, might not be the elite bucket-getter he was for most of his career. But he’s still brilliant at conducting highly efficient offense that pressures a defense’s pain points.

stories.title: Observations after Sixers shake off slow start, Embiid injury scare to win
stories.summary: The Sixers brushed off their blowout loss to the Celtics and got back in the win column Thursday night.
stories.detailText: Observations after Sixers shake off slow start, Embiid injury scare to win originally appeared on NBC Sports Philadelphia The Sixers brushed off their blowout loss to the Celtics and got back in the win column Thursday night. They overcame a first-quarter deficit as high as 17 points and earned a 123-112 home win over the Raptors. The Sixers moved to 10-3 and Toronto fell to 5-7. Tyrese Maxey had 27 points and eight assists. Joel Embiid added 20 points. Jaylen Brown tallied 18 points and six rebounds. VJ Edgecombe posted 15 points, eight rebounds and a season-high eight assists. Anfernee Simons scored 17 points and shot 5 for 6 from three-point range. RJ Barrett recorded 31 points and 14 rebounds. Immanuel Quickley had 26 points and six assists. The Sixers were without LeBron James (low back/sciatica management), Adem Bona (cervical spine sprain), Dominick Barlow (lower back stress reaction) and Ariel Hukporti (right Achilles tendon tear). The team told reporters Thursday morning that Bona will be re-evaluated in approximately one week and that Barlow participated in shootaround. The 23-year-old forward also went through a pregame workout on the Xfinity Mobile Arena floor. There’s no formal timetable for his return. Toronto’s sidelined players included Kawhi Leonard and Scottie Barnes. The Sixers will face the Pacers on Sunday afternoon in Philadelphia. Here are observations on their victory over the Raptors: Embiid exits early but returns to action Dean Wade began the game in James’ normal spot. The Sixers started slowly, missing their first foul field goals and opening 1 for 8 from three-point range. Embiid had an early injury scare. He stayed down after setting a ball screen and having an apparent knee-to-knee collision with Ja’Kobe Walter. The Sixers called timeout with 8:30 left in the first quarter and Embiid grabbed at his right knee. He eventually rose with assistance from teammates and Sixers head athletic trainer Kevin Johnson, then limped back to the locker room. Jabari Walker entered. At the 5:26 mark of the first quarter, Embiid checked back in to cheers from the home fans. “I knew that he didn’t twist it or anything,” Maxey said. “I knew it was a knee-to-knee, so I wasn’t too worried. He kept saying, ‘I just got kneed.’ That still hurts, though.” Embiid ended up logging 28 minutes, though he certainly wanted to play more. “He was very, very motivated to play,” Sixers head coach Nick Nurse said. “It was hard to get him out for his scheduled rests tonight, which is a good problem sometimes.” While Embiid’s return was a major positive development, the Sixers fell further behind. The Raptors’ lead swelled to 32-16 with a Jamison Battle three-pointer and Nurse burned a timeout. Brown-Edgecombe pair strong in 2nd quarter Simons sunk a buzzer-beating three to conclude the first quarter, cutting the Sixers’ deficit to nine points. “Those are big momentum plays that usually have some weight to them and carry you into the next moment,” Nurse said. The Sixers kept rolling against a shorthanded Toronto team playing on the second night of a back-to-back. Simons nailed a triple to kick off the scoring in the second quarter. Brown buried a mid-range jumper and Edgecombe jammed in a crowd-pleasing dunk to give the Sixers a 35-34 edge. Brown and Edgecombe shined in the second quarter both as individuals and as a duo. The Sixers need Edgecombe to attack a bit more offensively when he shares the floor with Brown and bench players. It doesn’t hurt for the second-year guard to have that clarity about his role in those units. “He’s one of our better playmakers,” Maxey said of Edgecombe. “He’s really good at getting downhill and creating for himself and others.” The Sixers’ only three bench rotation players were Walker, Simons and Kentavious Caldwell-Pope (11 points, five assists). In addition to Walker, Wade got center minutes behind Embiid. Maxey, Sixers pull away Embiid picked up his third foul with 2:23 left in the second quarter and had to take a seat. The teams were tied at 60 apiece through two periods. The game remained even for much of the third, but Maxey fueled an 11-0 Sixers run late in the quarter. His speed and the Sixers’ collective focus on pushing the pace whenever possible allowed the team to get regular points before Toronto could set its defense. Maxey zoomed in for a layup, then tossed the ball ahead to Brown for an easy bucket. Brown assisted a Simons three. Walker converted a fast-break lay-in and canned a three on the first possession of the fourth quarter. All of a sudden, the Sixers held a 101-87 lead. Brown, Edgecombe and the bench gave the Sixers more good minutes early in the fourth quarter. They sealed the deal without any late drama. And the fans chanting for a Tacko Fall appearance got their wish with a final-minute entrance by the 7-foot-6 center.

stories.title: Always one of a kind, Oubre reflects on Sixers stint, why he chose Pacers
stories.summary: Kelly Oubre Jr. reflected on his three seasons with the Sixers and discussed why he joined the Pacers.
stories.detailText: Always one of a kind, Oubre reflects on Sixers stint, why he chose Pacers originally appeared on NBC Sports Philadelphia The Kelly Oubre Jr. experience switched sides Sunday afternoon at Xfinity Mobile Arena. Back in Philadelphia with the visiting Pacers, Oubre was his usual self. There’s never any risk of mistaking Oubre for somebody else. “Love him,” Pacers head coach Rick Carlisle said pregame. “Such an upbeat guy. He’s such a unique person. Love the wardrobe, all the different stuff. He’s a very authentically one-of-a-kind type guy.” Carlise then detailed Oubre’s various basketball qualities, some of which he showed in Indiana’s 131-124 loss. The 30-year-old lefty wing scored 16 points and grabbed four rebounds. His day also included a theatrical imitation of Jaylen Brown’s off-arm push after the Sixers’ star was whistled for an offensive foul. Sixers fans grew familiiar with Oubre’s strengths, weaknesses and eccentricities during his three seasons as a Sixer. He wound up becoming the team’s third-longest tenured player behind only Joel Embiid and Tyrese Maxey. Oubre played 178 regular-season games and averaged 14.9 points, 5.4 rebounds, 1.6 assists and 1.3 steals. After the Sixers replaced president of basketball operations Daryl Morey with Mike Gansey , Oubre signed a two-year contract with the Pacers in free agency. “Mike came over from Cleveland and I heard whispers that he wanted some of his Cleveland guys,” Oubre said before the game in the visitors’ locker room. “And I was like, ‘OK, cool. I’m a Philly guy. So I guess when he comes over, I will no longer be a Philly guy.’ That was kind of the situation at hand. “No bad blood because business is business at the end of the day. They have a great team over there, and they put together a team that they think is the best for them. I’ll be all right elsewhere. I figured it out.” Oubre thought Indiana made sense as his next stop. “It was the pace, the culture, the attitude that this team has,” he said. “It’s a fast-paced style of basketball. It’s a bunch of guys who work collectively as a unit and kind of figure it out from there. “I thought that would be a great opportunity for me to come and and kind of free-flow play, not have to think. I was wrong. Been thinking a lot, but I’m starting to figure it out and starting to get my rhythm here. … It’s a great culture. Coach Rick Carlisle is a legend, Hall of Fame coach. And they wanted me. I love people who want me.” As Oubre settled into a new city, the Sixers had a stunning, transformational summer. Gansey traded for Jaylen Brown , signed LeBron James , and added veteran role players like (former Cavalier) Dean Wade , Anfernee Simons and Kentavious Caldwell-Pope. Oubre followed along. “It was must-see TV, like (for) everybody else,” he said. “As a basketball fan, it was pretty cool to see where I was kind of reinvent and get new life and new energy. So I was happy with that. Would I have loved to be a part of it? Of course. “But at the end of the day, I’m a grown man and I’ve got to keep it moving and figure it out for myself. It was entertaining. … I’m kind of happy for all the people that have sacrificed over these years. … I’m trying to put a road block in that road for y’all.” Oubre joined the Sixers on a minimum-salary deal in September of 2023 after averaging 20.3 points the past season with the Hornets. Head coach Nick Nurse pitched Oubre on his potential to be a valuable, multi-dimensional player for good teams. “I was literally about to be done with basketball,” he said. “Coach Nurse called me multiple times and said, ‘I want you to play for me.’ And I was like, ‘You know what? This guy really seems to care. He really wants me.’ So thank you for just pulling me out of that pit and that hole that I was in four years ago. I got some new life in my basketball career. “I’m always thankful for that and I love Nurse for that. Just appreciative for my time here. The battle wounds and scars that I’ve been able to build up, it made me a better man.” Throughout his Sixers stint, Oubre often spoke of growth, evolution, adaptation and self-discovery. He talked again Sunday about his desire to “Be water” and how life as a Sixer changed him. “I grew a lot, man,” Oubre said. “Just the mental fortitude of being able to withstand adversity. Being able to wake up and not necessarily know which soliders are going to battle, just having to put on different hats on any given night. At first it was challenging, because I’m thinking about all the logistics and things and like, ‘This is not what they asked me to do.’ But at the end of the day, I just bought into being somebody that can be like water and grow with the team. “It’s been a blessing to be able to play with (VJ Edgecombe), be able to watch Tyrese (Maxey) ascend. Those are the guys where we were front line a lot. Just going through war with those guys was amazing. It just taught me mental fortitude. If I can make it through this, I can make it through anything.” Oubre felt he developed a meaningful connection with the Philadelphia fan base over his three years. “When they talk about the City of Brotherly Love, I think they’re talking about your soul, not necessarily about what you can offer them and what you do,” he said. “Everybody in this city works hard. They wake up, go to work, keep the city going. And us as the prima donna basketball players, the least we can do is go hard and sacrifice for them so that they have something to cheer about when they come home from work. “I think that was the relationship that we had. I’m forever indebted and forever grateful to the people in the city of Philadelphia.”

stories.title: Barlow ‘making progress,' Embiid out vs. Pacers, more on Sixers
stories.summary: Dominick Barlow is trending up as he works his way back from injury.
stories.detailText: Barlow ‘making progress,' Embiid out vs. Pacers, more on Sixers originally appeared on NBC Sports Philadelphia Dominick Barlow decided to finish his post-practice workout Saturday with a windmill dunk. While Barlow remains out with a “lower back stress reaction” listing on the Sixers’ injury report, it’s one sign that he’s trending up in his rehab process. “He’s making progress,” Sixers head coach Nick Nurse said. “He was a part of the practice today. It’s kind of a game day type of practice … so it wasn’t super intense, as you might expect. But he was out there doing some stuff. He’s progressing. Just don’t know when he’ll be ready to go, but at least he’s making some progress now.” Barlow was one of the Sixers’ top role players last season, starting 59 games and contributing in a variety of areas. He averaged 7.7 points, 4.8 rebounds, 1.2 assists and 0.9 steals in 23.8 minutes per game. “Size, athleticism, rebounding,” Dean Wade said of the fifth-year forward. “He’s another guy that can switch one through five.” Whenever the 6-foot-9 Barlow is available for his season debut, the Sixers will welcome him back as another option at center. With Ariel Hukporti’s preseason Achilles tendon tear and Adem Bona’s cervical spine sprain, the team is light on healthy resources at the five. And Joel Embiid (right foot plantar fascia injury management) will sit Sunday afternoon vs. the Pacers on the first leg of a back-to-back. He’ll presumably return to the lineup when the Sixers visit the Nets on Monday night. “I think (Barlow) is probably going to have to play more five than we envisioned,” Nurse said, “but Jabari (Walker) is doing that as well. If the situation calls for that, I imagine that’s where he’ll help the most.” Blue Coats reps for Philon and Edwards With the Delaware Blue Coats hosting the Maine Red Claws on Friday and Saturday, the Sixers saw an opportunity for two players outside of the regular rotation to log minutes with their G League affiliate. Rookie guard Labaron Philon Jr. suited up Friday and third-year wing Justin Edwards played both games. Philon posted 20 points, nine rebounds and eight assists in a blowout loss. Edwards shot just 1 for 10 from the floor in the first game, but he scored 23 points on 9-for-17 shooting in Saturday’s win. Nurse has largely kept a tight rotation early in the season and the 10-3 Sixers haven’t had many lopsided games with ample garbage time. As of Saturday night, the Sixers ranked 29th in the NBA in bench minutes per game . “My first belief is it’s hard to get better unless you’re playing,” Nurse said. “That kind of trumps everything, in my opinion. Just historically, we’ve had a number of guys that have gone down to those games, respected it … and it’s really helped them in their careers. … It’s been a minute for these guys — both of them — since they’ve had any real court time. “So that fit into the schedule well. … I think it will also help them to just find some rhythm, find their legs a little bit. We’re going to need everybody at some point, so keep ‘em going.” VJ Edgecombe was among the crowd Friday night at Chase Fieldhouse. “They’re my brothers, man,” he said. “Labaron, Justin, (Caleb Love), (Rayan Rupert). I just wanted to show love. … I didn’t have (anything) to do yesterday. … We have that relationship off the court, too. I’m just being supportive and showing them that I care about them.”

stories.title: Paul George flips the script — and the bird — in Philadelphia return
stories.summary: PG-13, the former Sixer, poured in 36 points, then explained the baseline exchange that gave his return an R rating.
stories.detailText: Paul George flips the script — and the bird — in Philadelphia return originally appeared on NBC Sports Philadelphia PG-13 was rated R in his return to Philadelphia. The middle finger Paul George directed toward one baseline fan only reinforced that rating. Tuesday night was expected to revolve around Jaylen Brown and Jayson Tatum sharing an NBA court as opponents for the first time. Instead, the other headliner in the summer’s blockbuster trade stole the show. George scored a game-high 36 points in Boston’s 123-101 win over the Sixers. He shot 14 for 22 from the floor, made six of his 11 three-point attempts and scored 14 consecutive Boston points in the fourth quarter. The game was tied at 79 with 3:19 remaining in the third quarter. Boston outscored Philadelphia 44-22 from that point forward. The Celtics went nine minutes and 20 seconds without making a two-point field goal during the second half. Instead, they made nine consecutive field goals from three, the second-longest such streak by a Sixers opponent over the last 30 seasons. Payton Pritchard opened the fourth with consecutive threes. George followed with eight straight points, helping the Celtics begin the quarter on a 14-0 run that turned a competitive game into a rout. George’s return carried a complicated history. His two seasons with the Sixers were repeatedly interrupted by injuries, but he also played a significant role in their most memorable playoff run in years. Last spring, George helped the Sixers overcome a 3-1 deficit to eliminate Boston in seven games. He averaged 17.4 points and shot 55 percent from three during the series. Tyrese Maxey was happy to see his former teammate Tuesday, even if he disliked what followed. “It was good to see Paul,” Maxey said. “I love him, love his family. … He gave us everything he had while he was here. We know what he did in the playoffs last year. Great person, great family, and we’ll see him again.” Maxey then added one important qualifier. “I wanted him to score zero points.” George instead scored from nearly everywhere. “He had some open threes. He had some pull-up threes. He had some middies,” Maxey said. “He played within the game, too. That’s what Paul does. He plays within the game. He takes what the defense gives him, and we gave him too many open looks tonight. “PG, we know what PG does. We shouldn’t even be allowing him to get up 11 threes, and that’s on us.” Nick Nurse watched George attack the Sixers in several ways. “He really had it going,” Nurse said. “He’d post up, and-one, fallaways. He went down the lane, high archer off the glass, and-one. He scored in about every way he could tonight.” George heard boos during his return and said the arena carried the atmosphere, though not quite the intensity, of a playoff game. “This building can be very electric as well,” George said. “It was fun. It was fun to play in this environment.” One interaction extended beyond the usual reception for a returning player. During a stoppage, the ball rolled toward a fan seated along the baseline. George said the fan looked directly at him before dropping the ball instead of returning it. “There was a fan being an a–,” George said. “The ball rolled to him. He looked me dead in my eyes, dropped the ball on the ground as if I’m a dog to go fetch or go get it, instead of passing the ball to me like a normal fan would do. “And so, yeah, then I rolled him a middle finger in return.”

stories.title: James reaches assists milestone, keeps seeing plays ‘before they actually happen'
stories.summary: LeBron James showed his passing gifts Sunday and reached third in NBA history in assists.
stories.detailText: James reaches assists milestone, keeps seeing plays ‘before they actually happen' originally appeared on NBC Sports Philadelphia Tyrese Maxey admitted that he wasn’t entirely ready for LeBron James’ first pass of the afternoon Sunday. Maxey cut through the paint and James’ bounce pass was perfect, but the Sixers’ All-NBA guard missed his layup. He’s not fully accustomed yet to James’ precognitive gifts. “There’s still some times when you’re surprised,” Maxey said after the Sixers’ win over the Pacers. “… I was cutting through just to cut and create space. The ball hit me in the chest and I missed the layup. I was like, ‘Ah shoot, my bad.’ He was like, ‘Yeah, you weren’t looking.’” James has been trying to teach his teammates that he’ll spot openings they may not notice. “I just tell my guys, ‘Always pay attention to me when I’ve got the ball,’ because I definitely see plays develop before they happen,” James said. For the most part, James’ teammates adhered to his request on the latest historic day in a milestone-filled career. By setting up VJ Edgecombe’s layup with 1:19 left in the fourth quarter, James moved into third place on the NBA’s all-time assists list , passing Jason Kidd. The 22-time All-Star recorded 11 assists, his most so far as a Sixer, and now sits at 12,092 in his career. Chris Paul (12,552 assists) and John Stockton (15,806) are the only two players above James. “It’s obviously super humbling,” James said. “It’s something that I didn’t foresee in my career, but I knew assists meant a lot to me. Just the movement of the ball, being able to find my teammates, putting the ball on time and on target. “And also just being linked with some of the greats that have ever played this game and a dear friend of mine, J-Kidd. It’s really special.” James is at or near the top of many all-time leaderboards . He’s first in NBA history in points, games and minutes, sixth in steals and fifth in triple-doubles. Passing has always been a core element of his game. “First of all, he’s got the vision and the awareness,” Sixers head coach Nick Nurse said. “He’s got the size to see. I think he’s got some anticipation. Just a half-second before a play happens, he knows how the defense is moving. … And he throws crisp passes. Some of those are cooking out to the corner three guys, so it doesn’t let the close-out get there nearly as quickly.” James loves to pass, too. Whether it’s a long-range rocket, a drive-and-kick dish or a cross-court feed from the post that suggests he might have eyes in the back of his head, James has always enjoyed finding a wide range of ways to help his teammates. “For someone that talented, he’s very unselfish,” Maxey said. “He really prides himself on getting guys open.” As James recalled Sunday, he had exceptional passing tools long before he entered the NBA 24 seasons ago. “Since I was a kid, I’ve had the ability to see plays before they actually happen,” he said. “Seeing movement, seeing cracks in the defense before they were even open … it’s something that’s been with me since I was a kid. “I just had that vision and it just stuck with me throughout my playing days.”

stories.title: Sixers rule Brown out with hamstring injury for Magic game
stories.summary: Jaylen Brown will miss the Sixers' game Wednesday night against the Magic.
stories.detailText: Sixers rule Brown out with hamstring injury for Magic game originally appeared on NBC Sports Philadelphia Jaylen Brown will miss his second game as a Sixer on Wednesday night when the team meets the Magic in Orlando. The Sixers listed Brown as out with a left hamstring strain on their Tuesday evening injury report. Brown had a head-to-head collision with Julius Randle in the fourth quarter of the Sixers’ win Monday over the Nets. He returned after a few minutes of game action with a bandage on his forehead, but Brown exited again with 1:44 left and did not re-enter. Brown’s only other absence this season came in an Oct. 30 victory vs. the Knicks because of left knee patellar tendinopathy. He scored 31 points in both games of the Sixers’ latest back-to-back. For the season, the five-time All-Star wing has averaged 22.6 points, 6.6 rebounds and 3.6 assists. Dominick Barlow (lower back stress reaction) , Adem Bona (cervical spine sprain) and Ariel Hukporti (right Achilles tendon tear) all remain out for the 12-3 Sixers. The 6-7 Magic’s sidelined players include Paolo Banchero (right high ankle sprain) and Jonathan Isaac (left knee injury management).

stories.title: Observations after Sixers beat Bucks to move to 3-0, Embiid posts triple-double
stories.summary: The Sixers improved to 3-0 Saturday night by beating the Bucks at Xfinity Mobile Arena.
stories.detailText: Observations after Sixers beat Bucks to move to 3-0, Embiid posts triple-double originally appeared on NBC Sports Philadelphia The Sixers stayed unbeaten Saturday night at Xfinity Mobile Arena, earning a 127-116 win over the Bucks and improving to 3-0 on the season. Joel Embiid had his 10th career regular-season triple-double, tallying 28 points, 11 rebounds and 10 assists. On his 30th birthday, Jaylen Brown posted 27 points and five assists. Tyrese Maxey had 26 points. VJ Edgecombe scored 17 and grabbed 13 boards. The Sixers’ absences on the first night of a back-to-back included LeBron James (low back/sciatica management). Sixers head coach Nick Nurse said pregame that he did not know yet who would be available for his team’s matchup with the Pistons on Sunday. Here are observations on the Sixers’ victory Saturday: Wade debuts, Embiid starts in style Dean Wade made his Sixers debut and started in James’ place. He’d missed the first two games of the regular season with a left ankle sprain. The 3-and-D forward scored the night’s first points by a sinking a corner three-pointer on the opening possession. Embiid also had a sharp start. He moved well, made good decisions and served as the main hub of his team’s offense in the early going. The Sixers’ seven-time All-Star center has often enjoyed facing Myles Turner. He entered the night with an average of 29.4 points in 18 previous games against the Bucks big man. Embiid did a little bit of everything in the first quarter, posting eight points, four assists and four rebounds over nine minutes. After snatching an offensive board, Embiid drained a fadeaway jumper to give the Sixers a 10-1 lead. One of Embiid’s assists was quite stylish. He found Edgecombe open beyond the arc with a behind-the-back bounce pass. Edgecombe knocked down the shot and wound up going 3 for 4 from three-point range in the first quarter. Second-quarter struggles The Sixers added rookie Labaron Philon Jr. to their rotation. Jabari Walker stayed in the mix, though he didn’t enter until the 7:36 mark of the second quarter. Philon played four minutes in his NBA debut and missed his lone shot attempt, a corner three. On defense, Philon allowed a couple of blow-bys off the dribble. He generally looked like he belonged on offense, albeit without any production in his brief run. Maxey banked in a half-court heave at the first-quarter buzzer to put the Sixers up nine points. The Sixers couldn’t carry forward any momentum, however, and began the second quarter poorly. Adem Bona had another rough stint amid a subpar start to the season. After Anfernee Simons missed a transition layup try, Ryan Rollins’ three lifted the Bucks into a 40-37 lead. The dreadful stretch for the Sixers on both sides of the ball called to mind how they’d fallen into a 29-point deficit Thursday night vs. the Cavaliers before clawing out a comeback win. The Sixers mustered just seven points in first six minutes of the second quarter and had many stagnant possessions that concluded with contested jumpers. The team’s transition defense was dismal for much of the second period. Milwaukee had the game’s first 19 fast-break points. Star trio produces The Sixers regained the lead late in the second quarter. Kentavious Caldwell-Pope made two three-balls in the second and nabbed three first-half steals. Embiid assisted a go-ahead, and-one Walker layup. Brown hit a three with 11.8 seconds left in the second quarter. Unsurprisingly, his variety of shotmaking skills were useful without James in the lineup. Even when James or Embiid sit, the Sixers should have a simple advantage in terms of volume of stars over most opponents this year. stories.title: Bears QB Caleb Williams has moved on from 4-INT game, but frustration lingers
stories.summary: Caleb Williams spent his bye week resting his ailing hamstring, supporting his close friend Pete Crow-Armstrong as the Cubs outfielder was named NL MVP, and putting one of the worst games of his career in the rearview mirror.
stories.detailText: LAKE FOREST, Ill. -- Caleb Williams spent his bye week resting his ailing hamstring, supporting his close friend Pete Crow-Armstrong as the Chicago Cubs outfielder was named National League MVP , and putting one of the worst games of his career in the rearview mirror. The Chicago Bears went into their Week 10 bye with a 7-2 record after scraping by the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in a 27-24 win. Williams found redemption after throwing a career-worst four interceptions against Tampa Bay by leading his first winning drive of the season to set up Cairo Santos for a 38-yard field goal as time expired. Though the quarterback said he has moved past the interceptions, two of which he dubbed "funky" while calling another a "bad decision," the impact of his performance stayed with him during the time away. "The biggest thing is, the frustration comes from the feeling of, for me, personally, I always don't want to let my teammates down," Williams said. "That's always big for me. And in that situation, in those situations, I feel like I did. And so, that's the frustrating part that lingers." Williams' four-interception performance was an aberration over his three-year career. Before the game against the Bucs, the quarterback had thrown four total interceptions over his previous 11 games dating to Nov. 28. As the Bears gear up for the second half of their schedule, which features four NFC North games and meetings with AFC division leaders Jacksonville and Buffalo , the progress Williams has made earned high praise from coach Ben Johnson. "He's playing fast right now," Johnson said. "He's got a great approach. He's doing a good job downloading the game plan. We don't feel like we're hindered in any way as a coaching staff from the schematics of what we're able to put in, the details, the alerts. He's just able to digest a lot more. He's seeing coverage really well with where his eyes should be tied into his feet also. So, we're really encouraged with where he's at. We just got to continue to push that envelope and see how far it will take us." The Bears will need Williams at his best as they work through the league's toughest remaining schedule based on opponent win percentage. After entering its bye atop the NFC North, Chicago was in a three-way tie for first place in the division with Detroit and Minnesota by the end of Week 10. It was a stark reminder of how quickly things can change in a tight division race. In one week, the Bears went from No. 2 to No. 6 in the NFC playoff bracket. Chicago hosts New Orleans (3-6) on Sunday before turning around for a trip to Detroit on Thanksgiving Day. The Bears have yet to win a division game after early losses to the Vikings and Green Bay . "The pressure idea ... I don't think we have that here inside the building," Williams said. "I think that's the biggest thing is us understanding it only matters what we think, what we feel. You know one week we can be Super Bowl contenders, one week we can be playoff contenders, one week we can be wild-card contenders, one week we can be the worst team in the league and that comes from the outside noise and all that." The bye week allowed Williams to step away from the endless discussion around the Bears' Super Bowl prospects to celebrate the accomplishments of a fellow Chicago sports star. Williams was present last week for a star-studded dinner at Chicago steakhouse Adalina Prime to honor Crow-Armstrong, who was named the unanimous NL MVP after becoming the seventh player in MLB history to hit 40 home runs and steal 40 bases in a season. "That's one of the coolest things about being here in Chicago and what we're building here: It's not just Chicago Bears, it's us as Chicago athletes," Williams said. "We've talked about it multiple times, what we want to do for the city. This is just one of those stepping stones for Pete himself as his career goes, but also us as a friend group. We want to support each other, we want to show up for each other." Asked whether Chicago is big enough to handle two MVPs, a nod to the quarterback's fifth-best yet distant odds to win the award (+3500 according to DraftKings SportsBook), Williams didn't flinch. "Damn right," he said, smiling.

stories.title: Pair of ex-Seahawks safeties find new teams
stories.summary: D’Anthony Bell and A.J. Finley will be heading to new practice squads entering Week 11.
stories.detailText: A pair of former Seattle Seahawks safeties have made their way onto practice squads elsewhere, including someone who started on late notice earlier in the season. According to Tuesday’s NFL transaction wire, A.J. Finley signed with the Pittsburgh Steelers practice squad, having been released last week by Seattle. Finley was on injured reserve last season with a torn ACL suffered in training camp, and alternated between active roster and practice squad to start this year. He started in place of the injured Julian Love in Week 3 against the Washington Commanders, played exclusively special teams in Week 4 vs. the Los Angeles Chargers, but hasn’t had any playing time since then. Meanwhile, D’Anthony Bell has joined the Minnesota Vikings practice squad after remaining a free agent after the Seahawks let him go at the end of September. Bell was part of Seattle’s PS and active roster throughout 2025 as a special teamer and reserve safety, but when he was waived late in the year, the Carolina Panthers claimed him. Seattle nevertheless gave Bell a Super Bowl ring for his efforts . Seattle has had Ty Okada and Julian Love starting in tandem since Week 5, with Okada missing a month due to a hamstring injury. Rodney Thomas II has been the main reserve safety throughout the year, with Maxen Hook as additional practice squad depth.

stories.title: Officials who were bumped by reconfigured Week 10 schedule won't lose pay
stories.summary: The four officials who worked two games in Week 10 got paid accordingly.
stories.detailText: The four officials who worked two games in Week 10 got paid accordingly . The officials who found themselves without an assignment after the deck was reshuffled due to the ground stop won't be docked. NFL Referees Association executive director Scott Green tells PFT that the Collective Bargaining Agreement between the NFL and the NFLRA "requires that all active officials including anybody out with an injury are guaranteed 16 games of pay during the regular season regardless if they work all 16 games." Of course, it's possible that the NFL will reconfigure upcoming assignments to balance out the total assignments, putting an official who was supposed to work a given weekend on a bye while assigning an official to work when the official was supposed to be off. (That's not something Green said; it's our own assessment of how the imbalance can be rectified.) Hopefully, that won't happen. Those who were supposed to work but didn't should get credit for the game, since they were prepared to show up and do the job. And those who worked when they weren't supposed to shouldn't lose the opportunity to work their otherwise normal schedule — unless they choose that. And the four who worked two games in one day should absolutely get some sort of a bonus. As Green said, "[T]hat’s pretty remarkable as you are generally pretty wiped out both mentally and physically after working a game." The fact that Don Willard, Terry Killens, Jabir Walker, and Justin Larrew went above and beyond the call makes a reward not just appropriate but necessary.

stories.detailText: The San Francisco 49ers were anticipating a hostile environment when they entered AT&T Stadium on Sunday. That was, until it wasn’t anymore. A sea of 49ers fans took over the Cowboys’ stadium on Sunday and gave San Francisco a rare home-field advantage for a road game. The red-and-gold takeover was real. TRENT WILLIAMS: "We had to remind Brock in the huddle, like, 'Hey, Brock, it's silent in here, man. We can hear your voice. We don't need to have a silent count.'" (via @knbrmurph & @MarkusBoucher ) pic.twitter.com/mANjDjiHcC — KNBR (@KNBR) November 17, 2026 49ers offensive tackle Trent Williams celebrating with George Kittle. IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect 49ers offensive tackle Trent Williams, a Longview, Texas, native, said Sunday’s game “was like a dream come true.” “Walking down on that field, looking around, I’m like, ‘I’m struggling to find blue jerseys. A Cowboys fan.’ It literally looked like Levi’s. It sounded like Levi’s,” Williams told KNBR radio about the environment. Williams said the atmosphere was so pro-49ers that he reminded quarterback Brock Purdy that he didn’t need to use a silent count. For Dallas, it was the complete opposite. During the game, the rambunctious 49ers fan base was so loud while the team was on defense that Dak Prescott was forced to use a silent count. “We practiced all week going on a silent cadence, just assuming that the home crowd would have some impact,” Williams said. “We had to look at [Purdy] in the huddle and be like, ‘Brock, it’s Kyle in your head, man. We can hear your voice.’ … It was at that realization where I’m like, ‘Yeah, the Faithful took over.” Brock Purdy greeting Cowboys quarterback Dak Prescott after San Francisco won 46-40 on Sunday. AP Photo/Julio Cortez Williams wasn’t the only 49er to become aware of the surroundings. “I’ve been in this stadium a bunch, just coaching in the NFC East for a while,” Kyle Shanahan said to California Post sports reporter Evan Webeck. “For us not to have to use silent counts at all — I don’t even think we did on third down — was really cool.”

stories.title: The Rams’ season starts now
stories.summary: After a stretch of four winnable games, the real test starts now for Sean McVay’s Rams
stories.detailText: The Los Angeles Rams dug themselves out of a 2-4 hole en route to 6-4. They put together a four-game win streak. On the surface it seems like their early season struggles have all been corrected. In reality, their last four opponents have a combined record of 11-26-1. Cardinals 3-7 Chargers: 1-8 Commanders: 3-5-1 Raiders: 4-6 It’s reasonable to look at the last month’s schedule and conclude we really learned nothing about the Rams. Of course, they should be given credit for keeping losing teams losing. Who are the Rams following their recent rash of injuries? What happens when stiffer competition slows LA’s run game and they must rely on an inconsistent and short-handed passing attack? The defense has stymied offenses of late. What happens when they face the likes of Jordan Love, Patrick Mahomes, Brock Purdy, and Dak Prescott in the coming weeks? One thing is still true: the Rams have three lives left in the NFC playoff picture It will take 10 wins to make the playoffs. In other words, they cannot take more than three losses moving forward without leaving their destiny up to factors outside of their control. When looking on the horizon, LA’s season effectively starts out of their bye week. Week 11: BYE Week 12: vs Green Bay Packers Perhaps the single-most important game left. The Rams are competing directly with NFC West teams in the race for their own division, although the 49ers may be running away with it. They are also indirectly competing against the NFC North . This Wednesday night game is the perfect opportunity to ding Green Bay and bolster their own chances. It carries significant playoff weight. Week 13: vs Kansas City Chiefs Unimportant in terms of the NFC tiebreakers, although the Rams really cannot afford to use one of their remaining three lives this early. Week 14: at San Francisco 49ers Can LA avenge their Week 1 loss where they looked enitely unprepared to play. Week 15: vs Dallas Cowboys Dallas can light up the scoreboard. It will be a tough test for the defense. The offense may need more production than simply grounding the game out on the ground in order to keep pace. Week 16: at Seattle Seahawks It’s tough closing the season out with the Seahawks in two of the final three weeks. The silver lining is that winning both matchups would effectively eliminate Seattle and reinforce LA’s destiny. They must take care of business or they could be left on the outside looking in. (Photo by Todd Kirkland/Getty Images) | Getty Images One of the things that has been irritating many of us this season has been specific areas of offensive line play. I have seen people call out poor performances by Mike McGlinchey and Luke Wattenberg, but the real problem fans seem to see along the offensive line has been from interior guard Ben Powers. Personally, I’ve seen him whiff on blocks and get turned around so frequently that I wonder if he is the primary reason Bo Nix has been quick to bail to his right as often as he does. It’s not much better in the run game either, which is a source of constant frustration when watching these games. Head Coach Sean Payton was asked about making changes to the offensive line and he seemed to downplay it a bit, but left the door open too. “I made sure to make a point about evaluating all assets of what we’re doing in our front in the offense,” Payton said on Monday. “So I want to make sure one story doesn’t lead to another. We’ll spend an inordinate amount of time looking at mid-season cutups where we’re at relative to scheme and personnel.” Frankly, I think they should make a change. If it gets a lot worse, then you can always change it back. I have nothing against Powers, but he has struggled and it is problematic for sustaining offensive drives. Making a change shouldn’t be so hard to do. And maybe there are other things I don’t see or cannot understand due to being on the outside looking in. If it’s not Powers, then its someone in there not doing a good enough job and a change is certainly warranted. What do you think: is Payton waiting too long to take action along the line? stories.title: Week 11 Chicago Bears power rankings roundup
stories.summary: How are the Bears viewed after their bye week? @SamHouseholder has this week’s power rankings roundup.
stories.detailText: CHICAGO, ILLINOIS - NOVEMBER 08: D'Andre Swift #4 of the Chicago Bears reacts behind Alex Anzalone #34 of the Tampa Bay Buccaneers after rushing for a first down during the second quarter at Soldier Field on November 08, 2026 in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by John Fisher/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Chicago Bears are back in action following the bye week. It was great for the Bears to pause and have a chance to get healthy, but now is where the stakes are really going to go up. The schedule is full of playoff-hopeful teams, and that includes four more games against the NFC North gauntlet. Much is being made of Chicago’s Super Bowl chances after their 7-2 start. Now they actually have to go out and prove it. Let’s see where the Bears rank heading into their final eight games. WCG – Aaron Leming 4. Chicago Bears (7-2) Second-Half Outlook: Survive a brutal schedule down the stretch and hope that Jeffery Simmons continues to be a difference-maker Once dubbed a prime regression candidate heading into the regular season, the Bears have survived without Caleb Williams for three games and somehow continue to play much better defense than the numbers suggest. Williams’ Year 3 jump has been notable, even with a four-interception game in Week 9. The talent on offense is evident, and their ceiling feels safe with Ben Johnson calling plays. How far they go this season will come down to the defense, especially the secondary. We’ll see if not making another move at the deadline comes back to bite them. The Athletic – Chad Graff and Josh Kendall 6. Chicago Bears (7-2) Last week: 6 Sunday: Bye Breakout player: Luther Burden Ben Johnson was bullish about his second-year wide receiver in the preseason, and we’re seeing why. Burden is 16th in the league with 644 receiving yards, and 385 of those came in his last four games. From weeks 6 through 9, he had more receiving yards than all but five players in the league, and he got 23.5 percent of the Bears’ passing targets. That last number may go up as the season progresses. Pro Football Talk – Mike Florio Bears (No. 5; 7-2): They can’t afford to overlook the Saints, four days before a showdown with the Lions. Yahoo Sports – Frank Schwab 5. Chicago Bears (7-2, LW: 4) The Bears didn’t do anything wrong on their bye week. They didn’t “move down.” The Bengals just moved up after one of the most impressive games of the season. Lingering for the Bears is their home defeat to the Vikings in Week 2. They lost 9-3, and based on how the Vikings looked with Kirk Cousins in Week 10, that could be a problem. The Bears play at Minnesota in Week 18 and that’s looking like an early candidate to be flexed to the final Sunday night slot. Chicago is 0-2 in the division (Minnesota is 3-1) and that could also be bad for tiebreakers. The Lions suffered a massive injury to Aidan Hutchinson on Sunday and the Packers lost ground with a bad loss, so the NFC North could evolve into a two-team race. And the Bears might need to win in Minneapolis in Week 18 to take the division. NFL.com – Nick Shook 6. Chicago Bears (4) Having spent last week on a bye, the Bears didn’t do anything wrong — they just got caught up in a Power Rankings shakeup, with a couple of impressive teams leap-frogging them. Last time out, Chicago earned a narrow win over Tampa Bay that exposed some weaknesses but also felt like an anomaly in the larger picture. I still have plenty of confidence in this team, but it has to navigate the incredibly competitive NFC North to fulfill its potential. The Bears need to come out of the break on the right foot, facing a three-week stretch that includes dates with Detroit and Jacksonville. USAToday – Nate Davis 3. Chicago Bears (3): An offense that runs the ball more than any other in the league is about to get RB Kyle Monangai back − which is akin to making a trade deadline acquisition for free. ESPN NFL Nation – Courtney Cronin 4. Chicago Bears (7-2) Week 10 result: Bye Week 10 ranking: 4 Non-QB MVP at midseason: RB D’Andre Swift The Bears have maintained a top-five rushing offense (142 yards per game) despite a constant wave of injuries in the backfield. A big reason for that is the load Swift has carried in Kyle Monangai’s five-game absence (toe/thumb). Swift has logged the third-most offensive snaps of any Bears skill player (63%), including 22 rushes against the Patriots and 27 at Seattle a week later. He ran in three second-half TDs against the Seahawks, has already reached a career high of 10 TDs and is five away from setting the franchise’s single-season record. Despite dealing with injuries of his own, Swift has not missed a game. — Courtney Cronin CBS Sports – Pete Prisco 4. Chicago Bears (4) They entered their bye as one of the league’s hottest teams. Does it stay that way? There is nothing to think it won’t. What do you think of this week’s rankings? The idle week didn’t hurt them much, if at all.

stories.title: Arrest warrants issued for robbery of Steelers' Max Iheanachor
stories.summary: Arrest warrants have been issued for three individuals in connection with the burglary of the home of Steelers first-round pick Max Iheanachor, police said.
stories.detailText: PITTSBURGH -- Arrest warrants have been issued for three individuals in connection with the burglary of the home of Steelers first-round pick Max Iheanachor , the Pittsburgh police department announced Tuesday. Los Angeles residents Winter Brantley, 25, Andre Castle Jr., 23, and Lamar Stewart, 45, allegedly broke into Iheanachor's home in late August. Each faces multiple charges of burglary, criminal trespass, theft by unlawful taking, receiving stolen property and conspiracy, according to the police. According to the criminal complaint, Brantley is the sister of Iheanachor's roommate. Pittsburgh detectives are working with the U.S. Marshals Service in California to take the three into custody. More than $200,000 worth of jewelry and designer items were taken from Iheanachor's home in the Mount Washington neighborhood of Pittsburgh, police said in the release. Iheanachor was in New York for the Steelers' preseason finale against the Bills when the robbery occurred. Iheanachor's roommate, Ashley Brantley, told police in an October interview that he had been "beefing" with his sister on and off over the past year, according to the complaint. Detectives zeroed in on the trio with the help of security cameras in the neighborhood that spotted a dark Audi SUV at Iheanachor's residence on the day of the break-in, receipts for the credit card used to book the rental car used in the burglary and security footage at the Pittsburgh airport, per the complaint. Police added that the investigation is ongoing. Iheanachor, an Arizona State product selected with the 21st pick earlier this year, has started the Steelers' past seven games at right tackle.
