stories.detailText: One of the biggest shockers from the 49ers’ 46-40 road victory against the Cowboys on Sunday was the takeover of AT&T Stadium by San Francisco fans. Cowboys owner Jerry Jones appeared on “105.3 The Fan” on Tuesday morning and was asked his reaction to 49ers fans filling up his stadium and said, “That was not a shocker.” Jerry Jones sounded like he was trying to make excuses on why 49ers fans took over At&T Stadium: "Well I don't know if you saw the price of those tickets that they were paying… but it was unbelievable. I would say the highest price of any ticket, now I don't know this, but I… pic.twitter.com/oYC6QrirFV — OurSF49ers (@OurSf49ers) November 17, 2026 Jerry Jones downplays 49ers fans taking over AT&T Stadium on Sunday. AP Photo/Jeff Roberson “Well, I don’t know if you saw the price of those tickets that they were paying … but it was unbelievable,” Jones said. “I would say the highest price of any ticket.” Jones said the 49ers have “always had a way above-average attendance to our away games here in Dallas” and that longtime Cowboys season ticket holders blamed “this secondary market.” Jerry Jones meeting with members of the media following Sunday’s game against the 49ers. AP Photo/Jeffrey McWhorter “Many of our fans have seats licensed. So they technically own those seats,” Jones said. “For the most part, fans that have been out there for years, and years, and years. A lot of times, our ticket holders will maybe take two or three key games of the year and sell those tickets.” While Jones insisted that Cowboys fans price-gouged 49ers fans for their tickets, Dallas has certainly enjoyed a large turnout by its fans this season. According to ESPN, Dallas ranks first in the NFL for attendance , averaging 91,766 fans per home game. San Francisco averages 71,131 fans per home game. After the game, Jones was asked about the 49ers fans’ invasion and gave a defensive response : “We have a lot of [Cowboys fans] on the road ourselves.” San Francisco 49ers fans seen filling up AT&T Stadium during Sunday’s game. IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect That is accurate, too. ESPN reported that Dallas has averaged 73,450 fans per road game. Cowboys quarterback Dak Prescott was also aware of the sea of red in the seats and told reporters he “[t]ricked myself, told myself early the red was for my high school.” Prescott applauded the 49ers Faithful. “Their fans were more present than ours. But it created a great atmosphere, so take the good out of it one way or another. Leave it there.” San Francisco’s fans impacted Prescott’s offense, forcing Dallas to utilize a silent count.

stories.title: Lions create practice squad spot, set stage for Wednesday roster moves
stories.summary: The Detroit Lions have cut Ben Stille from the practice squad, setting the stage for several Wednesday roster moves.
stories.detailText: CINCINNATI, OHIO - AUGUST 13: Ben Stille #72 of the Detroit Lions walks off the field following the preseason game against the Cincinnati Bengals at Paycor Stadium on August 13, 2026 in Cincinnati, Ohio. (Photo by Justin Casterline/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Detroit Lions announced on Tuesday that they’ve released defensive lineman Ben Stille from the practice squad, creating a vacancy on the 17-man squad ahead of their week of preparation for the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. Stille, a 29-year-old veteran defensive lineman, was a standout during training camp this offseason, but he failed to make the 53-man roster. He was quickly signed to the practice squad and got the call-up for Detroit’s Week 1 game, playing just nine defensive snaps. This move sets the stage for what will likely be a few roster moves on Wednesday. How the Lions will fill the practice squad spot remains to be seen, but it is certainly worth noting that on Monday, the Lions waived cornerback Nick Whiteside to make room for waiver claim DE Tyrus Wheat . On Tuesday, Whiteside cleared waivers, so if Detroit wanted to bring Whiteside back, there’s now a spot on the practice squad for that. Whiteside spent two months on the Lions’ practice squad earlier this year. On top of that, the Lions are expected to activate safety Kerby Joseph from the Physically Unable to Perform list to the 53-man roster on Wednesday, the final day of Joseph’s 21-day evaluation window. If the Lions don’t activate Joseph, he would be shut down for the year, but on Tuesday, coach Dan Campbell indicated that Joseph will not only be activated, but they expect him to have a significant role in Sunday’s game against the Buccaneers . “The plan is to get him going. I think we’re going to let him play,” Campbell said. It’s not clear how the Lions will create the roster spot for Joseph, but the easiest way would be to place Aidan Hutchinson on injured reserve after he suffered a torn ACL on Sunday.

stories.title: Titans put WR Wan'Dale Robinson on IR due to ankle injury
stories.summary: The Titans placed wide receiver Wan'Dale Robinson on injured reserve Tuesday.
stories.detailText: NASHVILLE, Tenn. -- The Tennessee Titans placed wide receiver Wan'Dale Robinson on injured reserve Tuesday, which will keep him sidelined for at least the next four games. Robinson suffered an ankle injury late in Tennessee's 40-23 loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars on Sunday. He has 38 receptions for 272 yards and three touchdowns -- a team high -- this season after signing a four-year, $70 million contract in March to reunite him with offensive coordinator Brian Daboll. Robinson posted back-to-back 90-plus reception seasons in Daboll's offense with the New York Giants in 2024 and 2025. Robinson's absence comes as the Titans have played the past two games without first-round wide receiver Carnell Tate , who has been out with a shoulder injury. Tate, selected with the No. 4 pick this year, leads the Titans with 413 yards this season on 34 receptions. Tennessee signed receiver Xavier Restrepo to the active roster from the practice squad in a corresponding move Tuesday. Restrepo got the game-day elevation from the practice squad twice this season. He played 19 snaps after Robinson was injured and caught two passes for 31 yards. Restrepo signed with the Titans as an undrafted free agent out of Miami in 2025, the same year Tennessee selected Cam Ward with the No. 1 pick. In one year together at Miami, Ward found Restrepo 69 times for 1,127 yards and 11 touchdowns. Over his five-year career Restrepo finished as Miami's' all-time leader in receptions (200), receiving yards (2,844) and receiving touchdowns (21). He also holds the record for the most 100-yard games in Miami history. The Titans also signed wide receiver Jamari Thrash to their practice squad.

stories.title: Patriots Power Rankings: Pats plummet heading into Week 11
stories.summary: Check out how far down the ladder the experts dropped the Patriots heading into Week 11
stories.detailText: MUNICH, GERMANY - NOVEMBER 15: Fans enjoy the pre-match atmosphere before the NFL match between the New England Patriots and the Detroit Lions at the Allianz Arena on November 15, 2026 in Munich, Germany. (Photo by Sebastian Widmann/Getty Images) | Getty Images The league expressed it’s confidence in the Patriots recovering from their two-game blown-out streak, by removing them from the Week 12 Sunday Night Football lineup in favor of Raiders at Browns. Did you get that? A Patriots game has been replaced by the Raiders and Browns. In the immortal words of Dunder Mifflin’s Michael Scott, “Well, well well, how the turn tables…” The experts not only turned the Pats in the rankings after last week’s debacle of a game, but dumped them on their head. New England now sits at 20th and could conceivably fall lower after the Bye week, depending on the results of Week 11. With Drake Maye out, my guess is that the team will move forward with the quarterbacks on their roster: Tommy DeVito and the backup’s backup, Behren Morton. The coaching staff has two weeks to figure out how to stanch the bleeding on both sides of the ball. Maybe some of the walking wounded will heal up enough to contribute. I still think this team can potentially still win some games, even as banged up as they are. The Chargers (Week 12), Jets (Week 16) and Dolphins (Week 18) are still bad enough to be beatable. We’ll see. My expectations have dropped lower than the rankings, but I still want to watch to see how Mike Vrabel and his men handle the situation. GO PATS!! It will be a long bye week for Mike Vrabel, trying to fix his defense and hoping Maye will be himself when back healthy . [-2] 16th – Mike Florio (ProFootballTalk): It feels like the wheels are coming off . [-2] 17th – NFL Nation (ESPN): Non-QB MVP at midseason: RB Rhamondre Stevenson. The six-year veteran is one of the NFL’s best pass-protecting running backs, which has exceptional value when defenses have blitzed quarterback Drake Maye. Stevenson’s stat line isn’t eye-popping — 403 rushing yards, two rushing TDs, 27 catches, 259 receiving yards and two receiving TDs — but his determination to play through a knee injury in Week 10 reflects his team-first approach. On a team with few clear-cut candidates for this honor, that stands out . — Mike Reiss [-3] 19th – Ralph Vacchiano (FOX Sports): Getting drubbed by the Lions was bad enough, but the news that QB Drake Maye might be lost for the season with a fractured ankle is the real kiss of death for this battered, star-crossed team. This season has been both sad and predictable. Everyone knew the defending AFC champs would struggle with a much tougher schedule. Mike Vrabel’s offseason scandal put a big cloud over the Patriots, too. Then their injury luck ran out in a very big way. This bye is much needed. But they’ve lost three of four, are sitting at .500 (5-5), and can see the Bills, Vikings and Chiefs staring at them on their December schedule. They may not think it’s over, but it is. Stat To Know : With Drake Maye on the field, the Patriots averaged 6.00 yards per play and posted a 52.3% success rate, scoring 24 touchdowns on 545 plays. Without Maye, they only averaged 3.06 yards per play and posted a 37.3% success rate, scoring two touchdowns on 67 plays . [-4] 20th – Pete Prisco (CBS Sports): The Drake Maye injury has them way down here. They look done. Even with him, they weren’t playing great . [-8] 21st – Frank Schwab (Yahoo! Sports): The Patriots took a big drop in the rankings and it might not be far enough. Drake Maye suffered what the Patriots fear is a fractured ankle, per ESPN. At the very least he’ll be out a while and the most likely outcome seems to be that his season is over. That turns the offense over to Tommy DeVito. It has been a long time since he had a few decent games as a rookie for the Giants in 2023 and became a fleeting cult figure. He looked entirely overmatched Sunday after Maye left the game. He had 81 yards on 24 attempts against a bad Lions defense. Al-Shaair was inactive for Houston's 27-24 loss to the Cleveland Browns on Sunday because of a groin injury. "Not having Azeez is difficult for us. He's the heartbeat of our defense, does a lot for us -- communicating, leading, playing really well for us," coach DeMeco Ryans told reporters Tuesday. Henry To'oTo'o filled that role last Sunday with Shaair out and will continue in that role, Ryans said Tuesday. Shaair leads the Texans with 68 tackles in seven games. stories.title: Bears have a tough path to the playoffs, but are focused on 1-0
stories.summary: Ben Johnson and Caleb Williams met the media today and made it clear the Bears are focused on 1 thing.
stories.detailText: CHICAGO, ILLINOIS - NOVEMBER 8: Caleb Williams #18 of the Chicago Bears celebrates after a touchdown against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers during the first quarter at Soldier Field on November 8, 2026 in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by Todd Rosenberg/Getty Images) | Getty Images Welcome to SB Nation Reacts, a survey of fans across the NFL. Throughout the year, we ask questions of the most plugged-in Bears fans and fans across the country. The Chicago Bears may have dropped from the second seed to sixth in the conference standings during their bye, but they are still firmly in the NFC postseason mix at 7-2. The NFC North is the NFL’s toughest division, and the Bears (on paper) have the toughest remaining schedule, but Caleb Williams and the Bears aren’t looking ahead, and they’re 100% focused on the New Orleans Saints this Sunday. When asked how they stay in the moment and not get caught up in the division race and playoff positioning, Williams said , “The point of it is that we have to do our part, and our part is going 1-0 each week. I think that’s what it comes down to. You don’t focus on eight games from now because we haven’t played those eight games. You don’t focus on next week or the week after and who we got and prime times or the non-prime times.” ”You focus on being prepared for that moment of when the the ball gets snapped the first time, whistle gets blown, and we focus on being 1-0 that week. And then when the next one comes up, we’ll focus on being 1-0 that week. And if you go 1-0 each week and you focus on that each week, you’ll turn out to kind of be where you want to be at the end of it.” Head coach Ben Johnson also met the media today, and it’s not hard to figure out where Caleb’s 1-0 mindset comes from. When asked about his big-picture take on the NFC North, Johnson said , “It really doesn’t matter right now. Once again, it’s all about winning this week. So, we’ll worry about everything else when it’s time. It’s not time for that. There’s still eight games to be played, and this is the most important one because it’s the next one.” The Bears host the Saints on Sunday at Noon. stories.detailText: Despite being on their bye week , not everything is rest for the Cleveland Browns. Not only do fans need to change their plans for the Browns next game, which has been flexed to Sunday Night Football for Week 12 against the Las Vegas Raiders , but GM Andrew Berry rarely takes a week off from making changes to the roster. On Tuesday, Berry made three moves with Cleveland’s roster: Claimed DE Jamree Kromah off waivers from the Miami Dolphins Once again waived TE Carsen Ryan off the 53-man roster Waived DT Elijah Chatman off the injured reserve list Despite being on and off the active roster, Ryan has played in nine of the Browns 10 games this season, with 126 of his 129 snaps coming on special teams. Kromah is in his first season in the NFL after going undrafted out of James Madison. He played two games for the Chicago Bears and two with the Dolphins before being waived this week. His NFL draft profile was as follows: Kromah posted impressive impact production in 2023 after playing a bigger role than he had in the previous four seasons between Rutgers and James Madison. He’s muscular with very long arms and might have the frame for additional weight to bump inside. Kromah features jarring pop in his hands but might lack enough fluidity and athleticism to capitalize on it as a pro. He’s an effort rusher who is unlikely to create enough consistent pressure to warrant rush-down snaps, but he does have a shot at making the back end of a roster as a base end or future 3-technique. Chatman’s move was reported by Cleveland’s radio announcer, Andrew Siciliano: Browns waive DT Elijah Chatman from injured reserve. — Andrew Siciliano (@AndrewSiciliano) November 17, 2026 In two years in the NFL, Chatman played 22 games for the New York Giants before landing on the Browns roster this offseason.

stories.title: Source: Jordan Phillips latest Dolphins DT to suffer season-ending injury
stories.summary: Dolphins DT Jordan Phillips will miss the rest of the season with torn biceps, a source confirmed to ESPN.
stories.detailText: MIAMI GARDENS, Fla. -- Dolphins defensive tackle Jordan Phillips will miss the rest of the season with torn biceps, a source confirmed Tuesday to ESPN, adding to a string of season-ending injuries Miami has suffered over the past two weeks. Phillips left Sunday's loss to the Colts in the fourth quarter and did not return. Additional testing this week confirmed his diagnosis, and the team placed Phillips on injured reserve Tuesday. He is Miami's third defensive tackle to land on season-ending IR in the past two weeks, joining Zach Sieler and Zeek Biggers . The Dolphins' defensive tackle room is now the thinnest on its team, led by former first-round draft pick Kenneth Grant and Keith Cooper Jr ., who was signed from the practice squad last week. Miami also signed defensive lineman Jordan Jefferson to the active roster from the practice squad and added defensive lineman Matthew Butler to the practice squad. Grant and Cooper finished the game on the field for Miami against the Colts, who completed the quarter with 30 total yards in 13 plays. "They battled," coach Jeff Hafley said Monday. "In the fourth quarter, I think we had them go three-and-out two or three times to get the ball back to the offense. I give those guys a lot of credit, but it's hard when you're down to two guys there at the end of the game. It's hard with three because those guys rotate so much, taking on the double-teams and all the strain and the effort, so that was tough sledding against a good back yesterday." The Dolphins selected Phillips in the fifth round in 2025, and he quickly established himself as a rotational defensive lineman, playing 43.4% of their defensive snaps as a rookie. He took on a larger role this season and had played 60% of the team's snaps through nine games. Phillips, 22, is considered a key part of the NFL's youngest defense, which ranks 10th in yards allowed per game this season. After Sieler's injury in Week 9, Hafley mentioned Phillips as one of the players he expected to step up and lead Miami's defensive line room. "The way he plays, the way he goes about everything in this building," Hafley said. "I mean, he is a great example of leadership, and whether or not he's a second-year player only, it's going to be his time now to help out those other players." Beyond the trio of defensive tackles, the Dolphins placed quarterback Malik Willis on IR last week with a groin injury that Hafley said spread to his core. The team is hopeful Willis returns after missing a mandated minimum four games. Hafley said Monday that no surgery is planned for Willis at this time but that the decision is not final. In other moves Tuesday, the Dolphins signed quarterback Brady Cook and edge rusher Eric Watts to the active roster off the practice squad. Cook will back up interim starter Kyle McCord . Miami also added several players to the practice squad, including receiver Brady Boyd , defensive linemen Chris Smith and Matthew Butler and kicker Daniel Carlson . The Dolphins brought in Carlson to replace Zane Gonzalez , who was waived Monday after missing three kicks against the Colts. The Associated Press contributed to this report.

stories.title: Tuesday Miami Dolphins Thoughts With The Earl
stories.summary: If you were waiting for the opportune moment… that was it.
stories.detailText: INDIANAPOLIS, INDIANA - NOVEMBER 15: Michael Taaffe #16 of the Miami Dolphins intercepts a pass during the second quarter against the Indianapolis Colts at Lucas Oil Stadium on November 15, 2026 in Indianapolis, Indiana. (Photo by Justin Casterline/Getty Images) | Getty Images This game really depends upon your outlook for the season. If you are a “get the first draft pick at all costs” person, then you like this outcome. If you want to see a win and positive development, this was a horrible outcome. It was another of the “close, but no cigar” games the Dolphins have played this season. Here’s what I saw. THE DEFENSE HAD A MIXED REVIEW In previous games, there was a tradeoff between the offense and defense over which would show up. In this game, the offense was expected to be worse than the defense, with a backup QB getting his first-ever NFL action. However, the Dolphins still couldn’t go a game without some form of tradeoff. In this matchup, it was a tradeoff between the pass defense and the run defense. The Dolphins allowed a completion percentage over 70% and had a run defense that allowed less than 4 yards per carry. The pass defense had its best performance of the season. They held Danny Dimes to 50% completion and a 4.9 YPA average. They picked him off twice, one of which was returned for a TD. They allowed a passing TD and a couple of big plays but were solid in coverage. In a shock to everyone, the Dolphins allowed more rushing yards to TE Tyler Warren (3) than receiving yards (1). Warren was held without a catch until the 4th quarter and was a complete non-factor. Unfortunately, while the Dolphins pass defense stepped up covering the one receiving threat the Colts had, the run defense couldn’t stop the other threat the Colts posed. The Colts rushed for 172 yards on 34 carries, 106 of those yards coming in the 1st half on 19 carries. That’s a 5.6 YPA allowed. They improved a little in the second half, allowing 66 yards on 15 carries and a 4.4 YPA. But on the final drive, they allowed 12 yards on 2 carries that finished off the game. Just once, the team needs a complete performance on both sides of the ball. Now they need a complete performance on both sides of the ball. I will give them some due credit. They limited the Colts to 17 offensive points and were hamstrung by a limited offense, but the run defense was the backbreaker in this game. With the injuries mounting on the DL, I don’t know how they can fix it. SPECIAL TEAMS WAS UNACCEPTABLE We’ll get to the obvious problem in a moment. Bradley Pinion had 3 punts for 134 yards, with a 55-yarder. That’s an average of 44.7 overall and 39.5 on the other two punts. Indy’s punter had 6 for 290, averaging 48.3. The league average is 47.5. Miami still allowed too many yards in the kick return game. They had the 15-yard penalty on Louis, though I won’t complain about penalties since the total was lopsided in Miami’s favor and that penalty was ultimately inconsequential. It is still unacceptable, though. I said on Friday that the Dolphins simply aren’t good enough to win without winning in the margins. This is a young team working to find its identity. They come to work every day and put it all on the line every game. This isn’t the 2024 or 2025 Dolphins with players obviously checking out and Tua laughing on the sideline or Hill taking himself out of a game. This is a bad team playing like they are trying to get the top seed in the AFC. When the kicker, the second oldest player on the team, shanks not one, but two FGs and misses a PAT as the icing on the cake, that is a level of terrible that cannot be measured. After I watched the game and went to bed thinking of all I planned to say about how he cannot remain on the team if the coaches wanna keep the locker room, the Dolphins made my job easier and waived him on Monday. So that is a non-issue now. And I’ve seen the tweets about how the misses keep the tank alive and all that. But I cannot stress enough how not only is tanking a bad idea in general, but you really only tank for a QB, and the 2027 QB class is buns. They are bad. It’s an elevated class due to absences and wouldn’t be considered top prospects in a class like 2018 or 2020. I would love for the Dolphins to get Jeremiah Smith as much as any other fan. But this team is NOT trying to lose. They aren’t playing like they are trying to lose. They are talent deficient, but they aren’t tanking. So when you play as hard as they do and the veteran kicker can’t do the basic requirement of putting the ball through the uprights, then a message needs to be sent, and it was. THIS AND THAT Kyle McCord’s play will be dissected by many others, so I don’t want to get deep into it. I thought he played ok. I thought he played like a player getting his first NFL snaps. His performance isn’t worth getting worked up over one way or another. I said in Friday’s post that a healthy Willis wins this game by 2 scores, and I still believe it. But McCord played well enough for the Dolphins to get a win against another equally terrible team and was let down. The next step will be to see what, if any, level of improvements can be made. The run game has disappeared, and it probably won’t come back for a while. I tried to watch to see how much Indy loaded the box, but I didn’t truly keep track. Indy is a bad team, but Miami will face some good teams coming up; teams with solid to great defenses. My guess is they will load the box and force McCord to beat them. Having Meyer in there instead of Brewer hurt as well, but the OL can only do so much. The good news for the RBs is they were involved in the passing game. All three RBs were targeted 9 times with 8 catches for 62 yards, including the 4-yard loss for Kaytron Allen. If the RBs can contribute in the pass game, then the offense can function about as normally as we can expect. Even with the drop-off, Gordon is still on pace for a 1000 yard season. Caleb Douglas was invisible for most of the game but stepped up late. He will continue to be a force. Washington had the play of the game IMO with the one-handed catch down the sideline. He continues to improve in getting separation and being a factor in the offense. The TD throw was nice also. The TEs were invisible, and that’s a concern. I like Dulcich, and he has potential, but he is playing his way off the roster for 2027. The passing defense stepped up as I mentioned, and its leaders are two rookies. Michael Taaffe logged his 3rd INT this season, and Chris Johnson got his 2nd in consecutive weeks. It should have been his 3rd in 4 weeks, but that Jets WR fell down and they said Johnson interfered. He was a ballhawk in college, and it is showing up now. There are 17 players in the league with 3 or more INTs and only 7 with more than 3. Taaffe has the instincts to be around the ball a lot. His development going into the rest of this season will be interesting to watch. Regarding the kicker position, I would not be opposed to the Dolphins adding a young player – an undrafted rookie or second-year player – to fill the position. Vets are what they are, and while they offer some reliability, I’m all for giving a young player a chance to make his mark. They probably won’t because, well, they are trying to win games. But if they swing and miss with young players, at least they tried. If they get a hit, that’s something they can build on moving forward. I SAID WHAT I SAID Circling back to the opening paragraph, I am not a fan of losing games for a draft pick. I want the Dolphins to win. This game was frustrating because they had it and gave it away. They lost by the margins and lost the game. Unfortunately, this was the last win on the schedule for a while. Unless McCord magically turns into Tom Brady in the next few games, the Dolphins are looking at 1-16. They host the Jets in 2 weeks, but I don’t like that matchup with McCord. They host the hapless Chargers in week 16, and if Willis is back healthy, they’ll have a good chance of winning. They have the 8-1 Bills and 7-2 Broncos on the road in 2 of the next 3 games. They get the 7-2 Bears and 6-4 Packers, all battling for playoff seeding and that division title. Perhaps the Bills will lock up home-field advantage by week 17, and the Dolphins will get backups. Otherwise, the outlook is grim. To paraphrase Captain Jack Sparrow: if you were waiting for the opportune moment to get a win… that was it. We all knew this season wasn’t about the wins, but 1-16 is a tough mark for anyone. Even if the Dolphins go 12-5 over the next 2 seasons (they won’t), that is still 25-26 over 3 seasons. It’s going to be much worse than that. It is going to be a long road back to relevance for this franchise. I’ll cover that later on (either this week or next), so stay tuned.

stories.title: Nick Bosa’s shocking drought comes with a 49ers silver lining
stories.summary: The San Francisco 49ers hold an 8-1 record, the best in the NFC, and yet they still haven’t gotten quite the same type of production out of Nick Bosa that...
stories.detailText: The San Francisco 49ers hold an 8-1 record, the best in the NFC, and yet they still haven’t gotten quite the same type of production out of Nick Bosa that they’re accustomed to. NBC Sports Bay Area 49ers insider Matt Maiocco was asked if Bosa would ever be productive again and provided his insight on why he’s a key contributor to the 49ers’ pass rush. “Nick Bosa does not have a sack in the four games he has played this season. Never before has he gone four consecutive games in the same season without a sack since coming into the NFL in 2019,” Maiocco said. San Francisco 49ers edge rusher Nick Bosa during team warmups at AT&T Stadium. Getty Images Since Week 2 of last year, Bosa has missed an extensive amount of time dealing with a torn ACL last season and a calf injury this year. Maiocco added that Bosa not being able to participate in training camp this past summer put him behind the rest of his teammates, and then when he was cleared to play again, he played in two games, and then strained his calf. Bosa returned two weeks ago against the Raiders and recorded one tackle. He played 57 snaps against the Cowboys last Sunday, finishing without a tackle but registering a quarterback hit. Nick Bosa coming out of the tunnel before an NFL game against the Cowboys. Getty Images Maiocco added that Bosa is still winning despite the longest drought of his career. “Bosa leads the 49ers’ defensive line with a pass-rush win rate of 16.7 percent. That is down from past seasons, when he typically is around a 20 percent figure,” Maiocco said. On Monday, 49ers head coach Kyle Shanahan appeared on a conference call that included Maiocco, and he was asked if he was worried about Bosa and told reporters, “I’m not worried about Nick.” “Nick is going to get better each week, and he’ll eventually get there,” Shanahan said. While San Francisco is waiting for Bosa to reform himself, the 49ers defense can be patient. Nick Bosa attempting to tackle Raiders tight end Michael Mayer. Getty Images The 49ers rank second in the NFL in run defense, allowing 82.6 rushing yards per game. They’re also giving up an average of 21.8 points per game. Their pass rush has been inconsistent, especially Sunday, when the 49ers managed just one sack of Cowboys quarterback Dak Prescott, who threw for 343 yards and five touchdowns. The 49ers are tied with the Eagles for 30th in the NFL with 16 sacks, underscoring their struggles to get after opposing quarterbacks. Perhaps if Bosa can get back to his old self soon, he could give the 49ers’ pass rush the jolt that they desperately need.

stories.summary: The Lions have, in recent weeks, lost both linebacker Jack Campbell (neck) and defensive end Aidan Hutchinson (knee) to significant injuries.
stories.detailText: {"unknownError":"There has been an error","expiredError":"This video has been expired due to copyright restrictions.","unavailableError":"This content is not yet available.","georestrictedError":"This content is not available in your location.","networkId":"169843","adManagerUrl":"https://mssl.fwmrm.net/libs/adm/6.51.0/AdManager.js","serverId":"https://29773.v.fwmrm.net/ad/g/1","profileId":"169843:nbcu_web_jwp_cs_moat_https","afid":"140315314","caid":"nbcs_nbc_pft_reportcard_261117","csid":"nbcsports_embed_on_domain","sfid":"","adHocGroup":"","athlete":"","businessUnit":"NBC Sports","category":"No Ads","duration":"418885","event":"","externalAdvertiserId":"nbcs_nbc_pft_reportcard_261117","genre":"News, Trending","guid":"nbc_pft_reportcard_261117","league":"NFL","network":"","platform":"PC","playlist":"","show":"ProFootballTalk","sport":"Football","subtype":"","team":"Detroit Lions, Kansas City Chiefs, Houston Texans, Pittsburgh Steelers","title": "Week 10 report cards: Gibbs, Mahomes thriving","datePublished":"","videoPageUrl": "https://www.nbcsports.com/watch/nfl/profootballtalk/nfl-week-10-report-cards-jahmyr-gibbs-and-patrick-mahomes-are-thriving","availableDate":"2026-11-17T14:15:35Z","expirationDate":"","countries":""} The Lions have, in recent weeks, lost both linebacker Jack Campbell (neck) and defensive end Aidan Hutchinson (knee) to significant injuries. Coach Dan Campbell won't wallow in worrying about what may have been if the injuries hadn't occurred. "I think there's times where, if you're not careful, you lay in bed at night and you start thinking about all the 'what ifs,'" Campbell told reporters on Tuesday. "And at some point, you just become a miserable piece of shit. And I'm not gonna do it, man. We're not doing it. "I refuse to look at it that way. Does it sting? Yeah, it sure did in the moment. It's time to move on. We have to. "And what has happened with Jack Campbell and with Hutch now will not be in vain. We can't allow it to. They got us to this point. And so what are we gonna do about it, man? Are we just gonna let it go to waste, or are we gonna do something and pick up the slack?" It's the right attitude. Injuries happen. Sometimes, they happen to great players. (The more great players a team has, the greater the chances that one of them will be injured.) The only approach is to tap the next man up on the shoulder, expect him to do his job to the best of his ability, not allow it to become a "woe is us" situation, and keep going. That becomes easier, of course, if a team has quality depth. Which is why some teams that are top heavy with highly-paid stars find themselves in a pinch when those stars aren't available to play.

stories.title: Inside the Cowboys historic defensive collapse against the 49ers
stories.summary: Last week was so awful.
stories.detailText: Photo by Brian Rothmuller/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Dallas Cowboys lost a game to the San Francisco 49ers. That’s not a shocker to anyone, as this Cowboys team has struggled all season, and the 49ers are the best team they’ve played so far, and by a good margin. Looking at their opponents, San Francisco is the only offense the Cowboys have faced this year that is ranked in the top eight in scoring, now averaging over 31 points a game. In fact, the Cowboys haven’t fared well against offenses that average over 22 points a game. They’ve played five teams that average more than 22 points/game. Their record against those teams is 1-4. They’ve played five teams that average fewer than 22 points/game. Their record against those teams is 3-2. Clearly, playing decent offenses is not ideal for this Cowboys defense, so when they faced the NFC’s highest-scoring offense, it was a huge problem for a unit that has struggled immensely all season. Even so, it shouldn’t have been that bad. The defense gave up 584 total yards on the day. It was the most yards they have ever given up at home during their 67-year existence. The most ever is never good. The frustrating part about this game is that when you take a closer look, it’s easy to tell that the Cowboys never had a shot. The defense was just outmatched. It was like playing one of those games where you play against an older sibling, where they might toy around with you for a bit, only to flatten you when it’s time to get serious. The 49ers did that to the Cowboys’ defense. That doesn’t mean they were playing opossum at any point during the game. It’s just that whenever the 49ers found themselves in a crunch, they always had a go-to play where they knew they could take advantage of the Cowboys’ vulnerabilities. The Cowboys had several defensive breakdowns in the game, with multiple third-down letdowns and explosive plays. One of the most embarrassing plays came on the Deebo Samuel reverse play in the third quarter. When fullback Kyle Juszczyk went in motion, the entire defense was lured into a trance. Follow the Juice because that’s where the action goes most of the time. Only this time, the Juice wasn’t worth the squeeze. Sadly, the entire defense took the bait. It was crazy to see how many defenders continued chasing running back Kaelon Black. That left an entourage of blockers out in front of Samuel, leaving very little chance for the Cowboys to make a stop. Malik Hooker and Shemar James were the first to figure it out, but they were so far out of position that by the time they caught up, they were left gambling and taking poor angles. Cornerback Joey Porter Jr. was the last hope. He’s not the greatest tackler as it is, but he’s even worse when he’s washed out by multiple blockers. This one play shows how awful the Cowboys' defense is. Juszczyk goes in motion, trap set. Nobody recognizes Deebo swinging around. Defenders run themselves out of the play without a clue. Blockers heavily outnumber tacklers, and tacklers take terrible angles. Just pathetic. pic.twitter.com/qYISpQggww — Dan Rogers (@DannyPhantom24) November 16, 2026 In our game preview article , we mentioned that “Shanahanigans” would be an issue due to the Cowboys’ over-pursuing nature, and right on cue, they obliged. It was one of the poorest-defended reverse plays we’ve seen. Mental lapses are common for this defense, but more frustrating is when their effort is so lackadaisical. The touchdown run by the rookie Black was horrible for different reasons. It starts with Juice looping around with banana motion. He and wide receiver Jordan Watkins take on the outside defenders, leaving a nice hole for Black to run through. With no defenders to impede his path, Black gets a full head of steam and commits some terrible Big 10 rookie-on-rookie crime by running over Caleb Downs. Yes, that’s the Cowboys’ top draft pick being leveled, but in fairness to Downs, he squared up well. It’s just hard to defy physics when the running back comes plowing through with that much force. The rest of the Cowboys’ defense is sealed off from clever run-blocking that creeps to the second level. Cornerback Cobie Durant has one final chance to bring him down, but he gets run over like he’s not even there. It wouldn’t be a Cowboys game without a humiliating run-stop attempt against a team’s backup running back. This play is even more embarrassing. Juszczyk with the banana motion. He and Watkins take on the outside. Interior defenders are completely sealed off. Kaelon Black hits the hole and levels Caleb Downs. And he runs through Cobie Durant just for fun. Pathetic. pic.twitter.com/cDeJczzuIz — Dan Rogers (@DannyPhantom24) November 16, 2026 Getting their playmakers in space was the name of the game for the 49ers, and they did it often. They just meandered off to one side, got the defense to cha-cha-cha in that direction, and then boom, sealed off! On the quick pass to Samuel, the Cowboys’ defense was so out of position that their lone, helpless cornerback wasn’t even able to get a hand on him. When you go against a defense that lacks discipline, it's easy to find plays that work. All the skill players run to the left, the defense bites. Deebo has a convoy of blockers with only DaRon Bland to deal with. Bland is erased, Deebo waltzes in untouched. It's that easy. pic.twitter.com/5HUexZEuj9 — Dan Rogers (@DannyPhantom24) November 16, 2026 And then there were the two long touchdown passes to Christian McCaffrey. To be fair, McCaffrey is a handful all of the time, so game planning for him isn’t easy. The first touchdown catch was especially hard because the defense actually played well for 90% of the play. It was just hanging on for that last 10% that got them in trouble. McCaffrey was a sneaky sneakerton and, at the last second, leaked out into the secondary, and as soon as Brock Purdy saw that, it was over. The second touchdown was a harder pill to swallow for a couple of reasons. First, it essentially iced the game. Any hopes of a comeback were crushed. Second, in the defense’s biggest moment, they were once again escorted out of the play. It was a simple play for the 49ers, with all their receivers basically running away from where McCaffrey was, taking the defense with them. It was like Moses parting the Red Sea, only Kyle Shanahan was holding the staff, and it was the Cowboys’ defense that opened up for the easiest pitch-and-catch you’ll ever see. The first big touchdown to Christian McCaffrey was difficult to defend because Brock Purdy scrambled and extended the play. The second one, the Cowboys sold out with a blitz, and the 49ers schemed the defense completely out of the play. It was like shooting fish in a barrel. pic.twitter.com/jpgNn4AbcI — Dan Rogers (@DannyPhantom24) November 16, 2026 The Cowboys’ defense has been a problem all season, and the 49ers exploited every element of it. The same things keep happening, and they aren’t showing any sign of improvement. And it’s not going to get any easier with four of their final five games against offenses averaging over 22 points a game. This defense has fallen into troubling times with very little chance of escape.

teamStories.summary: Breaking down the tape from the No. 1 overall pick’s 1st start
teamStories.detailText: (Photo by Ethan Miller/Getty Images) | Getty Images Fernando Mendoza’s first NFL start in the Las Vegas Raiders’ Week 10 matchup against the Seattle Seahawks was a tale of two halves . In the first half, he completed 11 of 13 passes for 90 yards, with both incompletions being throwaways, and had five rushes for 21 yards and a touchdown. According to Sumer Sports , that resulted in a total EPA of 6.56, an EPA per play of 0.328 and a 55 percent success rate — pretty good numbers. However, the second half was a different story, going six-for-16 with 53 passing yards and one rush for one yard to post a negative 13.49 total EPA, negative 0.642 EPA per play and a 14.3 percent success rate. For the entire game, the No. 1 pick completed 17 of 29 passes (58.6 percent) for 143 passing yards, along with six rushes for 22 yards and a touchdown. That netted a negative 6.93 total EPA, negative 0.169 EPA per play and a 34.1 percent success rate. For more context, Pro Football Focus credited him with a 66.7 percent adjusted completion percentage (accounting for the two throwaways and one drop), a slightly below-baseline (60.0) 59.8 passing grade and a slightly above-baseline rushing grade (65.2) to sit at a 62.2 overall mark. While the numbers above help paint part of the picture, let’s dive into the tape to see the full story. Another boot with a free rusher Sees LB drop to take away the deep crosser (Nailor) Dumps it to Heyward to get 5 on 2nd & 6 pic.twitter.com/NwQQKXuGbn — Matt Holder (@MHolder95) November 16, 2026 To help get the rookie going, Klint Kubiak dialed up bootlegs on Mendoza’s first three throws. The clip above is the third one and is a great decision by the quarterback. His first read is to see if the go route from the outside receiver is available for a one-on-one opportunity. However, the Seahawks have that covered with the corner underneath and the boundary safety on top of the receiver to execute the Cover 2 side of the Cover 6 call. Mendoza’s next two options are either tight end Michael Mayer, who runs a chip release into a curl route, or wide receiver Jalen Nailor on a crossing/drag route. The MIKE linebacker is all over Mayer to take that away, and the WILL linebacker turns to ROBOT and help the corner against Nailor. Meanwhile, fullback Connor Heyward is working across the formation to sell the run fake and run a flat route. Heyward gets contacted by the edge rusher, who ends up getting pressure on Mendoza. However, Mendoza does a good job of going through his reads, finding Heyward and throwing around the free rusher to dump it to the fullback, who picks up five on second and six to set up a third-and-short situation. This isn’t a sexy throw by any means, but it’s a good process to put the offense in a favorable third down situation. The Natty play/TD run QB draw, great job setting up Spencer Burford's block to score pic.twitter.com/Ib95orsSYx — Matt Holder (@MHolder95) November 16, 2026 Here, we’ll get a look at the touchdown run that got Allegiant Stadium rocking and is eerily similar to the run the Indiana product had to win the National Championship over Miami last January. It’s third and 10 as the Raiders come out in an empty formation where the Seahawks respond with a five-man box and both safeties deep pre-snap. That’s the perfect look to run a quarterback draw into, and Mendoza sells it well by taking a drop with his first step and eyeing wide receivers Jalen Nailor and Tre Tucker post-snap, keeping the safeties in the end zone. Then, he takes off and does a great job of setting up left guard Spencer Burford’s block by getting downfield and pressing the five-yard line. That allows Burford to position himself between the linebacker and ball carrier. Finally, Mendoza shows off some impressive vision to see the field safety overpursue, cut back to the other hashmark and put the ball in the painted area. Best throw he had of the game Slant-Flat concept is covered Bails out of pocket with pressure up middle Can settle and hit White earlier, but eventually finds him on sideline for 22-yarder pic.twitter.com/5DKWS8PVlt — Matt Holder (@MHolder95) November 16, 2026 If the previous clip was the No. 1 pick’s best play of the game, the clip above is the best throw he made on the afternoon. Seattle starts with a two-high look pre-snap before rotating the boundary safety into the hook-to-curl area to play Cover 3. That takes away the curl from Nailor on the curl-flat concept. Maybe Mendoza can hit Mayer on the flat route, but the linebacker manages to avoid the pick and stay on top of the route. So, that’s a fine decision to hold onto the ball. But the problem is that the pocket starts to break down with Trey Zuhn III getting bull-rushed by Byron Murphy II. Mendoza manages to get out of trouble, but he can settle down and pick his eyes up at the 10-yard line instead of continuing to scramble. That would have allowed him to find slot receiver Cody White earlier — who is wide open on the corner route with a coverage bust from Devon Witherspoon — and hit White with some room to run. Regardless, Mendoza eventually finds White and delivers a strike on the run for a 22-yard gain near the sideline. Missed read/opportunity on the 4th & 1/1st & 10 debacle Boundary S rotates down to play Cover 3 Tucker beats press coverage and has a step on the CB for an explosive play but Mendoza doesn't let it rip Scrambles for 1 yard instead pic.twitter.com/w85mF2BoIC — Matt Holder (@MHolder95) November 16, 2026 This is where things started to get a little messy for the rookie, as the play above comes with about a minute left in the second quarter. Mendoza had a few missed opportunities for explosive plays in the game, with the one above being the biggest. The Seahawks show a two-safety coverage pre-snap but rotate into Cover 3 with the boundary safety spinning down. Since the Raiders are in a three-by-one formation, the boundary corner is locked in man coverage against Tucker, the Silver and Black’s best deep threat. Tucker beats press coverage and has a couple of steps on the corner, while the field or deep safety isn’t in a position to help the corner on a pass outside of the numbers. Mendoza gets to Tucker in his progression but doesn’t pull the trigger. Maybe left guard Spencer Burford losing control of Murphy discouraged the quarterback from letting it rip, but he has enough time and a clean enough pocket to make that throw. Instead, Mendoza opts to scramble and only picks up one yard. To be fair, this was the play that had the 4th and 1/first and 10 confusion (see the markers on the field and the scorebug on the top of the screen). So, maybe that played a factor in his decision, but this was certainly a missed opportunity. Sack, great blitz design by Macdonald OL and FB step strong with PA fake while WILL, MIKE & CB blitz weak Creates a numbers advantage for the defense and attacks 2 rookies (Mendoza & Washington) Mendoza's lack of feel for pressure shows up too pic.twitter.com/P9QP8rFx6O — Matt Holder (@MHolder95) November 16, 2026 Part of the reason Mendoza had such a low EPA is that he took six sacks on the afternoon. That was the result of some great play calling from Seattle’s defensive mastermind/head coach Mike Macdonald, and the rookie quarterback’s subpar feel for pressure. This is a perfect play call by Macdonald. Vegas runs a play-action pass where the entire offensive line and the full back work left to sell the run fake, while running back Mike Washington Jr. inserts into the protection scheme on the right edge. Meanwhile, Seattle slants the defensive line to the strong side of the formation as the MIKE and WILL linebackers blitz, on top of the cornerback coming off the edge. So, the Seahawks end up with a numbers advantage, where the Raiders have three blockers (Zuhn, right tackle DJ Glaze and Washington) to account for four pass-rushers (the edge, two linebackers and the corner). Also, Mendoza’s back is turned to the defense, and Kubiak calls a shot play with two deep routes. That being said, he gets turned around well before Witherspoon gets there and doesn’t sense the pressure coming, failing to move off his spot. Again, this is a tough look — especially for a quarterback making his first start. But if we back up to the pre-snap look, the safety playing outside the hashmark with the corner in press coverage was the tell that Witherspoon was blitzing, especially since the receiver is in a reduced or cut split (meaning between the numbers and hashmark). That creates a learning opportunity for the young QB. Mendoza slides protection right to account for the 4 pre-snap rush threats on that side But they all drop, Miller sticks with Murphy in the protection scheme/call while Witherspoon blitzes in C-gap Mendoza tries to throw hot but Witherspoon hits him when Jeanty turns his head pic.twitter.com/MfxaqpByrj — Matt Holder (@MHolder95) November 16, 2026 Another sack that highlights how Macdonald tested Mendoza’s ability to read the defense when the picture changes post-snap and handle pressure. Seattle comes out in a double A-gap look with a seven-man front, where four pass-rush threats are on the weak side of the offensive line (in this instance, the offense’s right side). So, the quarterback changes the protection, sliding it to the right. However, Macdonald doesn’t run a blitz but rather a simulated pressure, where all four defenders on the right side drop into coverage, and the nickel cornerback rushes through the C-gap for a four-man rush. Since the line is sliding right and there’s an edge rusher outside of the tight end, left tackle Kolton Miller stays with Murphy in the protection call, and Mayer sticks with the edge rusher, leaving Witherspoon unblocked as a free rusher. Mendoza doesn’t see or feel the pressure and ends up taking another big hit for a sack on third down. To be fair, it looks like he was trying to throw hot to Ashton Jeanty. But Witherspoon closed so quickly that he had already started making the tackle by the time Jeanty got his head around. Still, this is another instance where Mendoza needs to expect pressure with the nickel as close to the line of scrimmage as he is pre-snap. Makes the right read but doesn't quite finish the throw with the pocket collapsing Ball sails over Bech's head for an incompletion instead of a TD pic.twitter.com/9pS3Hh3IyO — Matt Holder (@MHolder95) November 16, 2026 Finally, Mendoza had a few throws where his accuracy got away from him, and the one above really hurt. On this play, it’s 2nd and 10 with about 2:45 to play and the Raiders trailing by 11. Seattle keeps the coverage pretty vanilla (for Macdonald’s standards, at least), playing Cover 6 with quarters to the wide side of the field near the goal line. Mendoza makes the right read since the safety steps inside while wide receiver Jack Bech runs an out route. That’s open for a potential touchdown. However, Mendoza doesn’t finish the throw, so the pass sails on him and falls incomplete. Granted, the pocket is collapsing, but he had enough room to deliver an accurate pass and just missed the opportunity. If you’re looking for more plays from Mendoza’s first start, dive into this thread I posted on X/Twitter .

teamStories.detailText: NFL flexes Raiders-Browns to NBC's Sunday Night Football, Patriots-Chargers out originally appeared on NBC Sports Philadelphia The NFL has made a Sunday night flex. The league on Tuesday flexed the Las Vegas Raiders-Cleveland Browns Week 12 matchup into NBC’s Sunday Night Football slot. It was initially slated for a 1 p.m. ET start. The New England Patriots – Los Angeles Chargers game that was initially set for primetime will move up to a 4:05 p.m. ET kickoff and will be on CBS. The NFL can flex games up to 12 days before they are scheduled, though Week 12 caused rarer challenges due to Thanksgiving week featuring more primetime games than usual. Despite making the Super Bowl last season, the Patriots have regressed after a 5-5 start. Quarterback Drake Maye is also now set for an extended spell on the sidelines, causing further issues for an ailing team. The Chargers have been one of the surprises of the season, but for all the wrong reasons. Justin Herbert and Co. went winless for their first eight games. They just finally took down a Jacoby Brissett-led Baltimore team to get to 1-8. Las Vegas will enter the matchup with No. 1 overall pick Fernando Mendoza taking over from Kirk Cousins, who was traded to Minnesota on deadline day. The 4-6 Raiders will be on primetime for the first time this season. Their last SNF game was in 2023. Cleveland is 6-4 and currently occupies the final AFC playoff spot as Deshaun Watson returns to form. The Browns are 4-0 at home for the first time since 1963, though they’ve eked out several close wins. Cleveland last hosted an SNF game in 2019. Its most recent SNF game was in 2021 at Baltimore, and its only other primetime game this season was a Thursday night Week 4 home win vs. Pittsburgh . The league also announced the Tennessee Titans-Jacksonville Jaguars game will move up to 1 p.m. ET.

teamStories.summary: How does every NFL team stack up heading into Week 11? We made our 1-32 list and picked the non-quarterback MVPs for each roster.
teamStories.detailText: When the NFL Honors awards ceremony takes place the Thursday before Super Bowl LXI , it's almost guaranteed that the player who accepts the MVP award will be a quarterback. Former Vikings running back Adrian Peterson (2012) is the only non-QB to be named MVP since 2010, and only three non-QBs have won in the 21st century. But what if quarterbacks were disqualified from winning the award? In addition to our weekly 1-32 rankings, we asked our NFL Nation reporters to pick the non-quarterback MVP for each team at midseason. Which defenders and skill players deserve love for what they've done this season? To form the 1-32 list, our power panel of more than a dozen NFL analysts evaluates how all 32 teams stack up against one another. Here are a couple of highlights from this week's rankings: The Patriots' trip to Munich could not have gone any worse, as they left Germany with a two-game losing streak and without quarterback Drake Maye ( ankle injury ). That caused them to tie for the biggest fall of any team in our Power Rankings over the past week (three spots), and Maye could be out for the season if his ankle is fractured. New England is 1-3 in its past four games, with all of its losses coming to NFC North opponents. The Browns are in the top 15 of our rankings for the first time this season after another comeback win -- this time against the Texans . Cleveland quarterback Deshaun Watson has conducted a winning drive in the fourth quarter or overtime in all six of the Browns' wins. Watson joins the Cowboys' Troy Aikman (1990) and Lions' Matthew Stafford (2016) as the only QBs in the Super Bowl era (since 1966) to achieve that feat, per ESPN Research. The Commanders made the biggest climb of any team this week (three spots) after a Thursday night win over the Giants. Washington is 2-1 since its bye week, and it's still not out of the NFC East race yet, two games behind first-place New York while owning the head-to-head tiebreaker with the Giants. However, the Commanders have only one divisional game left to boost their playoff odds -- Week 18 versus the Cowboys . Let's get into the full list, starting with a slight change at No. 1 from last week . Jump to a team: ARI | ATL | BAL | BUF | CAR | CHI | CIN CLE | DAL | DEN | DET | GB | HOU | IND JAX | KC | LAC | LAR | LV | MIA | MIN NE | NO | NYG | NYJ | PHI | PIT | SF SEA | TB | TEN | WSH 1. San Francisco 49ers (8-1) Week 10 result: Beat the Cowboys 46-40 Week 10 ranking: 2 Non-QB MVP at midseason: LB Fred Warner While QB Brock Purdy is a top candidate for league MVP , Warner is making a strong case to be the first linebacker to win Defensive Player of the Year since Luke Kuechly in 2013. Warner's 88 tackles rank sixth in the NFL. He's tied for first in forced fumbles (five) to go with a fumble recovery, 0.5 sacks and three pass breakups. He has done all that after returning from a broken and dislocated right ankle injury that cost him most of last season. For a defense on its fifth coordinator in five years, Warner is the constant and one of the primary reasons the Niners are 8-1. -- Nick Wagoner 2. Buffalo Bills (8-1) Week 10 result: Beat the Jets 31-12 Week 10 ranking: 1 Non-QB MVP at midseason: Edge rusher Greg Rousseau The transition from 4-3 defensive end to 3-4 outside linebacker has worked wonders for Rousseau. He is in the midst of a career season, leading the NFL in quarterback pressures (41) and quarterback hits (27). He is also tied for fourth in sacks (eight). Just over halfway through the season, Rousseau has already matched or set career highs in just about every meaningful pass rushing or defending stat. -- Nick Suss 3. Jacksonville Jaguars (7-2) Week 10 result: Beat the Titans 40-23 Week 10 ranking: 3 Non-QB MVP at midseason: WR Parker Washington Washington has been quarterback Trevor Lawrence 's top target -- his 64 targets are 21 more than the next-closest player ( Jakobi Meyers ). Washington has 36 catches for 645 yards and six touchdowns, which puts him on pace to set career highs in catches and receiving yards. There's a good chance he surpasses his previous best yardage (847) before December. He also leads the NFL with 17.9 yards per catch. Sunday's game specifically showcased the trust Lawrence has in Washington's ability to win 50-50 balls. -- Michael DiRocco 4. Chicago Bears (7-2) Week 10 result: Bye Week 10 ranking: 4 Non-QB MVP at midseason: RB D'Andre Swift The Bears have maintained a top-five rushing offense (142 yards per game) despite a constant wave of injuries in the backfield. A big reason for that is the load Swift has carried in Kyle Monangai 's five-game absence ( toe/thumb ). Swift has logged the third-most offensive snaps of any Bears skill player (63%), including 22 rushes against the Patriots and 27 at Seattle a week later . He ran in three second-half TDs against the Seahawks, has already reached a career high of 10 TDs and is five away from setting the franchise's single-season record. Despite dealing with injuries of his own, Swift has not missed a game. -- Courtney Cronin 5. Kansas City Chiefs (7-2) Week 10 result: Beat the Falcons 35-13 Week 10 ranking: 6 Non-QB MVP at midseason: RB Kenneth Walker III Walker has been a blessing for the Chiefs' offense, considering he has produced many of the team's explosive plays since signing a three-year deal this past offseason. He has generated 1,044 all-purpose yards, and his 11 total touchdowns are already his career high for a single season. By being a stabilizing presence, Walker has helped quarterback Patrick Mahomes find his groove following his return from the most significant injury of his career. Walker missed Week 10 because of a groin injury . -- Nate Taylor 6. Cincinnati Bengals (7-2) Week 10 result: Beat the Steelers 38-18 Week 10 ranking: 7 Non-QB MVP at midseason: OT Amarius Mims Not even pass block win rate, which is a great metric, does Mims full justice. According to NFL Next Gen Stats, Mims is in one-on-one blocking situations at the second-highest rate in the league (87.6%). Yet he has the lowest pressure rate allowed among all offensive tackles (3.1%). Coach Zac Taylor gave Mims the highest praise Sunday by saying he wouldn't trade him for any other right tackle. Given Cincinnati's offensive success on a high dropback rate, it's hard to argue with that. -- Ben Baby 7. Denver Broncos (7-2) Week 10 result: Bye Week 10 ranking: 5 Non-QB MVP at midseason: DT Zach Allen The Broncos are the league's foremost escape artists -- six of their seven wins have come by one score -- so we're looking for an MVP from the defense who has closed out those contests. Linebacker Alex Singleton leads the league in tackles per game and run stop win rate, but Allen's down-to-down relentlessness is the tone-setter for the group. He is second in the league in quarterback hits despite a double-team rate of 79.4% on his pass-rush snaps. Allen impacts almost everything happening around him. -- Jeff Legwold 8. Minnesota Vikings (7-2) Week 10 result: Beat the Packers 30-10 Week 10 ranking: 8 Non-QB MVP at midseason: Edge Andrew Van Ginkel There are multiple options to choose from on the Vikings' elite defense, and it's even reasonable to consider kicker Will Reichard . But Van Ginkel has been all over the field in coordinator Brian Flores' scheme. He leads the team in sacks (8.5) and pressure rate (15%) and is tied for the lead in forced fumbles (two). He has also been in coverage on 84 snaps, a high number for a player with such gaudy pass rush statistics. -- Kevin Seifert 9. Seattle Seahawks (6-4) Week 10 result: Beat the Raiders 21-13 Week 10 ranking: 9 Non-QB MVP at midseason: WR Jaxon Smith-Njigba Smith-Njigba would be Seattle's undisputed MVP even if quarterbacks weren't excluded, and the historic numbers he's producing should at least get him consideration for the leaguewide award. His 1,207 receiving yards are more than the rest of the team has combined (1,122). According to the Elias Sports Bureau, that's the highest percentage of a team's receiving yards (52%) through 10 games since 1966. It puts the reigning AP Offensive Player of the Year on pace to break Calvin Johnson's single-season record of 1,964. Smith-Njigba's 10 touchdown catches and 79 receptions also lead the NFL. He has been unstoppable despite Seattle's instability at quarterback, with Sam Darnold missing the better part of four games. -- Brady Henderson 10. Detroit Lions (7-2) Week 10 result: Beat the Patriots 35-10 Week 10 ranking: 10 Non-QB MVP at midseason: RB Jahmyr Gibbs There's a reason the Lions made Gibbs the NFL's highest-paid running back over the offseason. And he has proved to be worth every penny after a phenomenal start to his fourth season as the team's clear lead back. With 62 career touchdowns, the 24-year-old recently passed Hall of Famer Terrell Davis (61) for the most through a player's first four seasons in NFL history, per ESPN Research. His 1,384 scrimmage yards are the most a Lions player has produced through the first nine games of any season, and he has already scored 13 touchdowns. -- Eric Woodyard 11. Los Angeles Rams (6-4) Week 10 result: Beat the Cardinals 34-6 Week 10 ranking: 12 Non-QB MVP at midseason: RB Blake Corum With all the injuries the Rams have dealt with on offense, they've had to lean on their running back tandem of Corum and Kyren Williams . On Sunday, Corum ran for 100 yards and a touchdown on 17 carries and finished with a career-high 20 touches. It was his sixth straight game with a touchdown. Corum has been a key part of the Rams' rushing success during a four-game winning streak in which they've outrushed their opponents 653-175 (plus-478). According to ESPN Research, that is the team's largest rushing yards differential over a four-game span since 1984, the year Hall of Famer Eric Dickerson ran for an NFL-record 2,105 yards. -- Sarah Barshop 12. Green Bay Packers (6-4) Week 10 result: Lost to the Vikings 30-10 Week 10 ranking: 11 Non-QB MVP at midseason: WR Christian Watson When the Packers signed Watson to a four-year, $92 million contract extension this offseason, there were some whispers that they overspent to extend a receiver who had never had more than 620 receiving yards or seven touchdowns in a season. He had also never played a full season because of injuries. Now that Watson is third in the league in receiving yards (916) and tied for third in touchdown catches (seven), a deal that doesn't even rank him among the 20 highest-paid receivers in terms of average salary looks pretty good. -- Rob Demovsky 13. Pittsburgh Steelers (6-3) Week 10 result: Lost to the Bengals 38-18 Week 10 ranking: 13 Non-QB MVP at midseason: RB Jaylen Warren Even after a quiet night in the Steelers' blowout loss to the Bengals, Warren is still far and away the Steelers' MVP. He ranks sixth among all players in yards from scrimmage (1,039) this season and has a league-best 5.7 yards per carry. Warren also ranks fifth in rushing yards after contact (364). Given Pittsburgh's inconsistent and ineffective passing game, Warren is the Steelers' most reliable option to move the ball. -- Brooke Pryor 14. Cleveland Browns (6-4) Week 10 result: Beat the Texans 27-24 Week 10 ranking: 16 Non-QB MVP at midseason: CB Denzel Ward The Browns' defense hasn't taken a big step back without two-time Defensive Player of the Year Myles Garrett or former coordinator Jim Schwartz, and Ward is a big reason. Cleveland is still playing the highest rate of man coverage in the NFL, and Ward's ability to shut down half the field gives coordinator Mike Rutenberg the confidence to use that man-heavy approach. Ward leads the Browns with three interceptions and is allowing 3.8 yards per target, the third fewest among corners with at least 30 targets, according to NFL Next Gen Stats. -- Daniel Oyefusi 15. New York Giants (5-3-1) Week 10 result: Lost to the Commanders 24-21 Week 10 ranking: 15 Non-QB MVP at midseason: TE Isaiah Likely Likely has had success with Jaxson Dart , Jameis Winston and J.J. McCarthy at quarterback. He has already set a new career high with 575 receiving yards. The Giants' offense wouldn't be nearly as good if he wasn't their first free agent signing . Likely has also been incredibly consistent, with at least 50 receiving yards in six games and just one drop. That, as well as Likely's team-high seven touchdowns, are the differentiators that put him ahead of wide receiver Malik Nabers for this honor. -- Jordan Raanan 16. Houston Texans (3-6) Week 10 result: Lost to the Browns 27-24 Week 10 ranking: 17 Non-QB MVP at midseason: Edge Will Anderson Jr . Despite the Texans' defense regressing drastically from last season, Anderson is currently at the top of DraftKings' odds for Defensive Player of the Year (+120). He has 39 combined tackles (21 solo, 18 assists), 10.5 sacks, two forced fumbles and one fumble recovery. His sack total leads the league, and he's tied for 12th among edge rushers with a 22.6% pass rush win rate. -- DJ Bien-Aime 17. New England Patriots (5-5) Week 10 result: Lost to the Lions 35-10 Week 10 ranking: 14 Non-QB MVP at midseason: RB Rhamondre Stevenson The six-year veteran is one of the NFL's best pass-protecting running backs, which has exceptional value when defenses have blitzed quarterback Drake Maye . Stevenson's stat line isn't eye-popping -- 403 rushing yards, two rushing TDs, 27 catches for 259 yards and two TDs -- but his determination to play through a knee injury in Week 10 reflects his team-first approach. On a team with few clear-cut candidates for this honor, that stands out. -- Mike Reiss 18. Tampa Bay Buccaneers (3-6) Week 10 result: Bye Week 10 ranking: 18 Non-QB MVP at midseason: S Tykee Smith The Bucs' third-year safety is having another strong season in coverage, producing two interceptions and three pass deflections. But more importantly, he has assumed a leadership role that the Bucs have noticed -- and one that is necessary in a defense that deploys several rookies. With safety Antoine Winfield Jr in and out of the lineup because of injury , Smith has helped Tampa's defense rank 10th in passing yards allowed per game (213.8). -- Jeremy Fowler 19. Carolina Panthers (4-5) Week 10 result: Beat the Saints 20-17 Week 10 ranking: 19 Non-QB MVP at midseason: RB Chuba Hubbard Hubbard carried the Panthers' offense Sunday with 172 total yards and two rushing touchdowns. He's on pace to eclipse career highs in every major statistical category this season, and he's considered the flagbearer for the locker room. He has already topped the bulk of his production from his forgettable 2025 campaign in just nine games. Quarterback Bryce Young is in the middle of a career year, but it's clear that Hubbard is the tone-setter for Carolina. And he is making an inconsistent offensive line look good. -- Mike Kaye 20. Dallas Cowboys (4-6) Week 10 result: Lost to the 49ers 46-40 Week 10 ranking: 20 Non-QB MVP at midseason: DT Quinnen Williams Considering the porous nature of the Cowboys' defense, it's difficult to say a player on that unit deserves this honor, but that's how well Williams has played. He leads the team with six sacks, the most for a Dallas defensive tackle in a season since 2017, and is second in QB pressures. Williams leads the NFL with 15 tackles for loss and is tied for fifth with three forced fumbles. He is doing everything he can to raise the level of play on defense. He just needs more help. -- Todd Archer 21. Washington Commanders (3-5-1) Week 10 result: Beat the Giants 24-21 Week 10 ranking: 24 Non-QB MVP at midseason: LB Sonny Styles The seventh pick in April's draft has made an instant impact with his speed and smarts. Styles leads Washington with 80 tackles -- nobody else has more than 55. He has recorded one sack, forced a fumble and intercepted a pass. His speed has helped stop big plays, and his pre-snap diagnosis even led to a crucial tackle for a loss in Week 10. Styles is still learning and has certainly made mistakes, but he has provided Washington a defensive player to build around. -- John Keim 22. Las Vegas Raiders (4-6) Week 10 result: Lost to the Seahawks 21-13 Week 10 ranking: 21 Non-QB MVP at midseason: TE Brock Bowers Bowers has played on another level in his third season. Until Sunday's loss, which he had to leave early because of an ankle injury , he had seven straight games with 70-plus receiving yards. He has also recorded at least 100 receiving yards in three contests. Bowers' season is even more impressive when factoring in how a lot of his production has come from being lined up on the outside. He has run 96 routes from the outside, totaling 27 catches for 409 yards and four touchdowns on 36 targets. -- Ryan McFadden 23. Atlanta Falcons (3-7) Week 10 result: Lost to the Chiefs 35-13 Week 10 ranking: 23 Non-QB MVP at midseason: RB Bijan Robinson No surprise here. Robinson is third in the league in rushing yards (951) despite going over 80 yards just once in the Falcons' past five games. He is also third in scrimmage yards (1,207) despite posting only two games of 40 or more receiving yards since Week 1. Robinson has a team-leading six touchdowns and has done it all despite shaky offensive line play. Robinson has 216 yards over expectation, second only to the Chiefs' Kenneth Walker III, per NFL Next Gen Stats. -- Marc Raimondi 24. New Orleans Saints (3-6) Week 10 result: Lost to the Panthers 20-17 Week 10 ranking: 26 Non-QB MVP at midseason: Edge Chase Young Young and Carl Granderson rank fourth (eight) and second (8.5), respectively, in sacks this season. But Young gets the nod here for the key plays he has made that aren't just sacks. He ranks 24th out of 133 qualifying edge rushers in pass rush win rate (21.9%) and is well on track for beating his career high of 10 sacks. Young would likely be receiving a lot more recognition if the Saints had a better overall record. -- Katherine Terrell 25. Baltimore Ravens (4-6) Week 10 result: Lost to the Chargers 23-20 Week 10 ranking: 22 Non-QB MVP at midseason: WR Zay Flowers It has been such a disappointing season that it's difficult to pick any valuable Ravens. Flowers has been one of the few players who have exceeded expectations for Baltimore, but he had a costly fourth-quarter fumble Monday night. His production has been impacted by injuries at quarterback. In 10 quarters with Lamar Jackson , Flowers has looked like one of the most dangerous wide receivers in the NFL, catching 16 passes for 353 yards (22.1 per catch) and two touchdowns. In 26 quarters with Tyler Huntley , Joe Fagnano and Jacoby Brissett , Flowers has totaled 33 receptions for 335 yards (10.1 per catch) and one touchdown. -- Jamison Hensley 26. Arizona Cardinals (3-7) Week 10 result: Lost to the Rams 34-6 Week 10 ranking: 25 Non-QB MVP at midseason: TE Trey McBride Well, for starters, McBride is the only playmaker still standing. He's getting all the attention from opposing defenses with receiver Marvin Harrison Jr . traded to Houston, quarterback Jacoby Brissett traded to Baltimore, receiver Michael Wilson out for the season because of a neck injury , and running back Jeremiyah Love on IR because of an ankle injury . McBride has 78 catches for 635 yards and five touchdowns. He has carried the Cardinals' offense as far as it has gone this season, but he doesn't have a lot of help at the moment. -- Josh Weinfuss 27. New York Jets (2-8) Week 10 result: Lost to the Bills 31-12 Week 10 ranking: 27 Non-QB MVP at midseason: WR Garrett Wilson Wilson has been frustrated at times by his usage, but he's still on pace for 1,125 receiving yards -- which would be a career high and his fourth 1,000-yard season in five years. He's a bright spot on an offense that has gone nine straight quarters without a touchdown. The Jets should use him more in the red zone; he has only eight targets, one reception and one touchdown on plays inside the 20. Wilson is 26 years old and signed through 2030. He should be a foundational player for the team, but there's always the fear that he will ask to be traded to a winning squad. -- Rich Cimini 28. Philadelphia Eagles (2-7) Week 10 result: Bye Week 10 ranking: 28 Non-QB MVP at midseason: P Braden Mann Mann has been called on more than any other punter, which is what happens when your offense leads the league in three-and-outs by a healthy margin. But he has been nails for the most part. Mann has an NFL-best 22 punts inside the 20-yard line and only two touchbacks. His 86-yard boot in Week 9 against the Giants was the second-longest punt since 2000. And no, it is not a good sign when your punter is your first-half MVP. -- Tim McManus 29. Indianapolis Colts (3-7) Week 10 result: Beat the Dolphins 24-22 Week 10 ranking: 29 Non-QB MVP at midseason: RB Jonathan Taylor Even amid the Colts' dysfunction, Taylor has managed to be among the NFL's better running backs. He hasn't had the trademark 50- and 60-yard touchdowns, but he currently ranks fourth with 22 explosive runs (10 yards or longer). Taylor's 73.9 rushing yards per game is the lowest of his career. But considering the added attention from defenses because of the lack of a consistent passing game, and the recent trade of All-Pro guard Quenton Nelson , things could be a lot worse. Taylor remains the Colts' biggest playmaker. -- Stephen Holder 30. Miami Dolphins (1-8) Week 10 result: Lost to the Colts 24-22 Week 10 ranking: 30 Non-QB MVP at midseason: LB Jacob Rodriguez The Dolphins' 2026 second-round pick introduced himself to the NFL with 14 tackles in Week 1, and he hasn't slowed down since. Rodriguez is tied for second among all rookies in tackles per game (8.9); he has forced a fumble, intercepted a pass and broken up four others. Rodriguez has worn the green dot for the Dolphins all season, which shows how much trust Miami's new regime has in him as a foundational player for its defense. -- Marcel Louis-Jacques 31. Los Angeles Chargers (1-8) Week 10 result: Beat the Ravens 23-20 Week 10 ranking: 32 Non-QB MVP at midseason: Edge Tuli Tuipulotu It's hard to find value in the Chargers' one-win debacle, but the defense has at least been passable. And there's no doubt that Tuipulotu is the best player on that unit. The 2023 second-round pick has a team-high 22 pressures and is tied for the team lead with three sacks. His average run tackle comes after a gain of just 2.2 yards. -- Aaron Schatz 32. Tennessee Titans (1-8) Week 10 result: Lost to the Jaguars 40-23 Week 10 ranking: 31 Non-QB MVP at midseason: RB Tony Pollard Pollard has posted a gain of 30-plus yards in each of the past three games. And with 628 rushing yards so far, he is on his way to more than 1,000 yards for the fifth consecutive season. General manager Mike Borgonzi said he'd like to keep the 29-year-old back after his contract expires at the end of the season. The Titans see Pollard as a big part of QB Cam Ward 's development. "To have a guy like Tony who can move the pile, gain first downs with his legs, keep us in advantageous situations with regards to down-and-distance is always beneficial for the quarterback," coach Robert Saleh said. -- Turron Davenport
